name: @signal8ai/mcp

tools.name: search_companies
tools.description: Search for companies by name or ticker symbol in the Signal8 database. Returns matching companies with their ticker, name, CIK, and exchange.

query.description: Search query - company name or ticker symbol (e.g., "Tesla", "TSLA")

tools.name: get_company_profile
tools.description: Get an enriched company profile by ticker symbol. Returns CIK, exchange, sector, industry, market cap, employee count, description, and other fundamental data in a lightweight response. Includes halted/haltCode/haltedAt trading-halt status on every call (false/null when trading normally); a halted-but-listed ticker reports delisted:false. `sharesOutstanding` is dated: `sharesOutstandingAsOf` + `sharesOutstandingAsOfKind` ("stated" = the issuer's statement date; "checked" = when it was last confirmed against a vendor; "none" = date not recorded) and a vendor-free `sharesOutstandingSource`. The count is only meaningful with its date. A null count means not measured; it does not mean zero. `cik: null` is a foreign issuer listed on US OTC that files nothing with the SEC (e.g. PGPHF): name, exchange and country come from reference data and every field Signal8 lacks is null.

tools.name: get_quote
tools.description: Get the current stock quote for a company: price, volume, change, market cap and other real-time market data. Trading-halt fields halted, haltCode, haltReason, haltedAt and resumptionAt are present on every response (false/null when trading normally); a halted ticker returns the last-known quote instead of an error, or currentPrice null with halted true when nothing is recoverable. `priceAsOfDate` is the ET date the price printed (`priceAsOf` the trade time when known), not when it was read; null means the print date was not measured. `priceIsStale: true` means the price is an older held close (the last trade on that date), not a current trading price. `quoteSource: "screener_reference"` (foreign listings on US OTC that file nothing with the SEC, e.g. PGPHF) means `currentPrice` is a vendor reference price whose print date is not known, and every other market field is null (not measured). `marketCap` is the live price times the SEC-derived share count; when that count is unavailable it is null with `marketCapWithheldReason` set, which means not measured, not zero and not "no market cap". The count is `sharesOutstanding`, dated by `sharesOutstandingAsOf` and `sharesOutstandingAsOfKind` ("stated" = the issuer's statement date; "checked" = when it was last confirmed against a vendor; "none" = date not recorded), with a vendor-free `sharesOutstandingSource`. When no measured count exists, `sharesOutstanding` and `marketCap` are a best estimate (the newest dated filed or reference count, moved onto today's split basis): `sharesOutstandingEstimated: true`, `sharesOutstandingEstimateKind` and `marketCapEstimated: true` with `marketCapAsOf` (the count's date). Kind "stated_as_of" is the issuer's last stated count, a dated point rather than a bound or today's count; later issuances recorded in the filings are listed in `statedAsOf.events`, not added to it ("at_least" is the retired name of the same state).

tools.name: get_market_metrics
tools.description: Get computed market metrics for a company: volume averages, volatility, simple moving averages and trend direction, beyond the basic quote.

tools.name: get_short_interest
tools.description: Get short interest data for a company: short volume, short ratio, days to cover and short percent of float. A null `shortInterestPercent` always carries `shortInterestPercentReason`: "float_not_point" means the float on record is a bound or estimate, and a percent-of-float is not computed from a bound or estimate; "float_unavailable" means no float of any kind is on record; "short_pct_of_float_unreconciled" means a point float existed but the ratio was implausible or the split basis could not be resolved; "float_class_scope_mismatch" means the float on record pools more than one separately listed share class (e.g. Class A plus Class D) while short interest is reported for this symbol's class only, so the two figures are not comparable. A null percent means not measured; it does not mean 0%.

tools.name: get_float
tools.description: Get float data for a company: floatShares, floatDefinition, the as-of date and, when the headline float is withheld, the bounds and labelled stand-ins that replace it. Null, absent or withheld means not measured; it does not mean "no float", "no restricted shares" or zero. A numeric 0 is a measured zero, so the reason and marker fields ("floatWithheldReason", "restrictedBlockCount", "provenance", "direction") carry the verdict, not the value alone. The share count the float was judged against ("basisSharesOutstanding") is dated by "sharesOutstandingAsOf" and "sharesOutstandingAsOfKind" ("stated", "checked", or "none" = date not recorded) and "sharesOutstandingSource". "floatDefinition": "tradeable" (shares outstanding minus affiliates minus restricted/unregistered blocks; filing-derived snapshot tickers), "non_affiliate" (the SEC I.B.6 figure, which includes restricted shares held by non-affiliates and is not a trader's float), "non_affiliate_estimate" (from ownership filings), "free_float" (vendor). "floatDefinition" and "source" appear only on snapshot results; an absent floatDefinition means the figure is not a filing-derived tradeable float. "nonAffiliateFloatShares" (snapshot tickers) is the input that baby-shelf / I.B.6 math rests on; it is not tradeable supply, and the tradeable float is not an I.B.6 input. Precedence: when the snapshot carries any figure ("floatEstimate", "tradeableFloatCeiling", an "affiliateBasis" range), "floatShares" stays null and that figure is the answer. A lower tier fills "floatShares" (its own "source" and definition, with "snapshotFloatWithheldReason" as provenance context, not a second refusal) only when the snapshot has no figure, or its only figure is a trivial ceiling (at or above 99% of the share count), which is stripped. Floors, points, every "shares_outstanding_ceiling" and an "affiliate_sizing_estimate" (with its "reason" and "unsizedAffiliates") are kept. A lower tier that also answered appears as "otherSourceFloat" {floatShares, source, provenance:"other_source", floatDefinition, asOfDate}: a secondary other-source figure, not the float and not an input to arithmetic. A lower-tier figure that predates a split the snapshot names, predates recorded issuances of 10% or more of it, or falls outside the snapshot's bounds is refused: "fallbackRefusal" {reason, refusedSource, detail}. "floatShares" null with "floatWithheldReason" set and no lower-tier figure means no source could answer. A point (bound "point", or a "floatEstimate" with "statedAsOf" {asOf, source, events[]}) is a plain number as of asOf, with the unsized later issuances in "statedAsOf.events" as its caveat. A ceiling, floor or range is not a float figure: it means the filings put the float at most or at least N. Stand-ins on a withheld result are not floats and are not inputs to a market cap, percent-of-float, short-interest ratio, screen, sort or comparison. (1) "tradeableFloatCeiling": the tradeable float is at most this (null = no bound, not 0). (2) "affiliateBasis.floatLowerBound" / "floatUpperBound": a range for the non-affiliate float (still including non-affiliate restricted shares); each end is null independently; on a published float it is context only. (3) "floatEstimate" {shares, basis, direction, confidence, rung, bound, asOf, reason, qualifier, offBasis, statedAsOf, staleness}: "basis" says what it rests on; "direction" "overstates" = the true float is at most shares, "understates" = at least, "unknown"; "rung" names the ladder step; rung "best_estimate" is the most likely figure when every filing rung withheld ("basisKind" = what it rests on, "assumptions" = how each unsized holder was treated), an estimate and not a measurement; "qualifier" is the caveat that belongs with the figure. "offBasis": "pre_split_as_filed" (as of asOf, before "splitsAfter" [{ratio, effectiveDate, status}]), "ordinary_shares_unconverted" (ordinary shares, not ADSs), "count_predates_issuances" (dated cover count "countSource", later issuances uncounted); an offBasis figure is accurate only with its label and is not comparable with a price, market cap, another float or a threshold. "staleness" flags a point older than 12 months or post-dated by a known issuance. An estimate never becomes floatShares. Unrelated to the boolean "floatEstimated" (a published floatShares back-derived from a USD public-float disclosure). (4) "vendorFallback" {floatShares, provenance:"vendor", floatDefinition:"free_float", asOfDate, splitAdjusted}: a third-party free float as of its date, not Signal8's float. "restrictedShares" null means not measured (a block exists whose size the filings leave unstated), not zero; "restrictedBlockCount" 0 is a measured answer. "affiliateBasisStale" (basisSpanDays, affiliateAnchorDate) labels an affiliate table materially older than the share count. "tradeableBasis": "convention_conservative" means a published convention resolved the figure (see "tradeableConvention"), so it is not exact.

tools.name: get_float_history
tools.description: Get the point-in-time float history for a company: one sample per trade date (float shares, shares outstanding, and the source the float came from), showing the float on a past date and how it expanded across a dilution event. The series is forward-only: it began accumulating in mid-2026 and is not backfilled, so early or absent history is expected and an empty rows array is a normal result, not an error or a sign of delisting. Each row carries "source" ("computed", "sec_10k" or a market-data vendor tier) because float quality varies by provider.

days.description: Lookback window in trade dates. Default 90, clamped to 1-730.

tools.name: get_historical_prices
tools.description: Get historical OHLCV price candles for a stock at daily, weekly or monthly resolution, for a period shorthand (1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y, 5Y or the full history) or an explicit from/to UNIX timestamp window. The default is one year of daily candles.

period.description: Lookback period shorthand (default: "1Y"). Ignored if from/to are provided.

from.description: Start date as UNIX timestamp (overrides period)

to.description: End date as UNIX timestamp (overrides period)

tools.name: get_stock_price_change
tools.description: Get percentage price changes for a stock across multiple timeframes (1D, 5D, 1M, 3M, 6M, YTD, 1Y, 3Y, 5Y, 10Y and MAX) without full candle data.

tools.name: get_financials
tools.description: Get income statement, balance sheet and cash flow data for a company (revenue, profitability, debt, cash position), in annual, quarterly or trailing-twelve-month views.

type.description: Financial period type: "annual", "quarter", or "ttm" (trailing twelve months). Defaults to annual.

limit.description: Maximum number of periods to return (1-40). Defaults to 8.

tools.name: get_earnings
tools.description: Get historical earnings data for a company: EPS actual vs estimate, revenue actual vs estimate, and surprise percentages (beats and misses).

limit.description: Maximum number of earnings periods to return (1-40). Defaults to 8.

tools.name: get_executives
tools.description: Get the key executives and officers of a company: name, title, compensation and tenure.

tools.name: get_news
tools.description: Get recent news articles, press releases and AI-analysed SEC filings for a company. Filing rows (category "sec_filing") are event-bearing forms only (8-K, 6-K, 424B prospectus supplements, S-1/F-1, 10-K/10-Q/20-F, SC 13D, proxies, delisting notices; never Form 3/4/5, 13G or bank-note 424B2) and carry formType and accessionNumber; a filing that repeats a press release is omitted in favour of the release. For a small foreign issuer that files its news as 6-Ks, the filing is the news. `pressReleasesOnly` returns only official company press releases (no filings).

limit.description: Maximum number of articles to return (1-20). Defaults to 10.

pressReleasesOnly.description: When true, return only official company press releases (exclude third-party news).

tools.name: get_analyst_consensus
tools.description: Get the analyst ratings consensus for a company: average target price, number of analysts, buy/hold/sell breakdown and consensus recommendation.

tools.name: get_analyst_estimates
tools.description: Get forward analyst estimates for a company: EPS, revenue, EBITDA and net income (low/high/avg) with analyst counts, for annual or quarterly periods.

limit.description: Maximum number of estimate periods to return (1-40). Defaults to 8.

tools.name: get_clinical_trials
tools.description: Get the ClinicalTrials.gov trials Signal8 has matched to a company: phase, status, conditions, interventions and key dates. The list includes trials the company leads and trials where it is only a collaborator on another organisation's study. Each trial carries metadata.sponsorRole ("lead", "collaborator", or null = not determined) and metadata.sponsor (the lead sponsor). Only lead trials are the company's own pipeline; a collaborator trial is a trial run by the named lead sponsor that the company collaborates on. `sponsorRole: "lead"` filters to the company's own trials. The response's total, leadTotal and collaboratorTotal count the full list, so a total above the returned count means the list was truncated. Dates of type ESTIMATED are sponsor projections, not facts.

limit.description: Maximum number of clinical trials to return (1-50). Defaults to 10.

sponsorRole.description: Filter by the company's role: "lead" (its own trials), "collaborator", or "all" (default).

tools.name: search_clinical_trials
tools.description: Search clinical trials market-wide (across companies), filtered by phase, indication, sponsor, status and date window, with sorting and pagination. An unrecognised phase, status, dateField or sort value is rejected with the allowed list (it is never silently ignored). A result's ticker is the company whose trial list the row was collected under, which may be the lead sponsor or only a collaborator; metadata.sponsor is the lead sponsor, so a row is that ticker's own trial only when metadata.sponsor is that company.

phase.description: Comma-separated phases, matching ANY of them. Allowed tokens: EARLY_PHASE1, PHASE1, PHASE2, PHASE3, PHASE4 (also accepted: "Phase 2", "2", "Early Phase 1"). Example: "PHASE2,PHASE3". A combined "Phase 2/Phase 3" string is rejected; each phase is a separate token.

indication.description: Comma-separated condition names, exact match (case-sensitive), e.g. "Breast Cancer"

sponsor.description: Case-insensitive substring of the LEAD sponsor name (collaborators are not searched)

dateField.description: Date column the from/to window applies to (default primary_completion_date)

from.description: Inclusive start: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD

to.description: Inclusive end: YYYY, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD (a partial date covers its whole year/month)

tools.name: get_top_movers
tools.description: Top stock movers: gainers (largest % up), losers (largest % down), or active (highest volume). Optional session window (premarket / regular / afterhours; regular default; not supported for active). An optional date (YYYY-MM-DD) returns a past trade date's gainers/losers on a historical daily close-to-close basis (computed from split-adjusted daily bars, not intraday); session is rejected when date is set, date is not supported for direction=active, and a non-trade date (weekend/holiday) returns an empty list (not an error). Penny-stock artifacts are filtered by default; includePennyStocks=true includes sub-$1 movers.

direction.description: Mover direction: gainers, losers, or active (volume)

limit.description: Optional max rows (1–100). Backend default applied when omitted.

session.description: Session window: premarket (4:00–9:30 AM ET), regular (RTH close-to-close, default), afterhours (4:00–8:00 PM ET). Live-only; rejected (400) when combined with date.

includePennyStocks.description: Loosen penny-stock artifact guards. Default false enforces prev_close >= $1 and a $1M dollar-volume floor. Set true to allow sub-$1 movers (prev_close >= $0.10, no dollar-volume floor). The ABS(change_pct) <= 500 cap applies in both modes.

date.description: Optional past trade date (YYYY-MM-DD). When set, returns that day's top gainers/losers computed on a historical daily close-to-close basis from split-adjusted daily bars (NOT intraday, NOT session-specific). Rejected with 400 when combined with a non-regular session or with direction="active"; a future or malformed date is also 400. A weekend/holiday date returns an empty list, not an error.

tools.name: get_market_news
tools.description: Get the latest market-wide news across all tickers, most recent first (not filtered to one company). Every item is significance-classified at ingest (critical | major | standard); the default filter of critical,major is the "top stories" view. Served by the /news/latest public endpoint (added 2026-07-29; 404 on a backend without it).

limit.description: Maximum items to return (1-50). Defaults to 10.

significance.description: CSV of levels to include, e.g. "critical,major" (default) or "critical,major,standard".

tools.name: get_market_breadth
tools.description: Get market breadth aggregates (advance/decline counts and ratio, percent of constituents above their 50DMA and 200DMA, and counts of new 52-week highs/lows) for a chosen universe (sp500, ndx, or all): a snapshot of overall market state.

universe.description: Universe to aggregate over: sp500, ndx, or all (default sp500)

tools.name: get_trading_halts
tools.description: List securities currently halted across NASDAQ/NYSE/AMEX (from the consolidated Nasdaq Trader halt feed). Each halt includes ticker, market, haltCode (T1/T2/T12/LUDP/H10/...), human-readable reason, haltedAt, haltAgeDays, and the scheduled resumptionAt when one is set. `halts` holds halts that began within the last 30 days; `longRunningHalts` holds older halts the feed still lists (often regulatory halts that have lasted months or years); they are not new halts. `asOf` is when the list was read. An empty list is a normal state (no active halts right now), not an error. Halt rows carry no price.

tools.name: get_earnings_calendar
tools.description: Get upcoming and recent earnings releases between two dates. Optionally restrict to a list of tickers. Returns ticker, date, time (BMO/AMC), EPS estimate, and revenue estimate when available. Supports market cap filtering to focus on large-cap or small-cap earnings only.

minMarketCap.description: Minimum market cap in USD (e.g., 10000000000 for $10B+)

maxMarketCap.description: Maximum market cap in USD (e.g., 2000000000 for under $2B)

tools.name: get_economic_calendar
tools.description: Get scheduled macro/economic events (CPI, FOMC, jobs reports, GDP, etc.) between two dates. Optionally filter to a single country (ISO-3166 alpha-2, e.g. "US"). Defaults to US when omitted.

tools.name: get_filing_calendar
tools.description: Get the forward-looking 10-K / 10-Q SEC filing-deadline calendar within a date window. Optionally restrict to a universe (sp500/ndx/dji/all) and/or a list of form types (default both 10-K and 10-Q).

formTypes.description: Optional SEC form types subset, e.g. ["10-Q"]

tools.name: get_post_earnings_movers
tools.description: Get stocks that moved significantly after earnings reports on a given date. Returns pre-computed price changes joined with earnings surprise data, one row per ticker. Includes preEarningsClose, currentPrice, changePct, EPS/revenue actuals vs estimates, and surprise percentages. Filter by minimum absolute % change threshold.

minChangePct.description: Minimum absolute % price change to include (default 5). Set to 0 for all.

tools.name: get_recent_material_filings
tools.description: Recent material 8-K filings (last 7 days) for the constituents of an index universe. By default returns the high-signal 8-K item codes (material agreements, M&A, executive changes, restructurings, etc.); pass `items` to filter to specific 8-K item codes. Choose the universe with `universe`.

universe.description: Index universe to scan (sp500, ndx, or dji).

tools.name: screen_sec_filings
tools.description: Screen SEC filings across all companies with company-level filters (sector, industry, market cap, exchange) combined with filing-level filters (form type, date range). Returns filings enriched with company metadata: ticker, sector, industry, exchange, market cap, and price. Answers questions like "all S-1 filings from biotech companies under $500M market cap" or "recent 8-K filings from Technology sector companies". Results are filings, not a company universe or a company count. Only the 500 largest matching companies by market cap are searched (narrower filters reach smaller ones). Filters for float, price, company type, foreign issuer, recent IPO, full-text queries and 8-K item codes are not available here. Coverage: Signal8's SEC EDGAR archive, updated through the day, in its held range (see `archiveFrom` in each response; currently from late 2021, expanding back to 2016 as the history backfill fills in). Before archiveFrom it holds only a scatter, so absence before archiveFrom is not evidence a filing was never filed; SEC EDGAR itself covers earlier periods. Record-only rows (bodyStored: false) have no stored body; the document is at its sec.gov URL.

industry.description: Filter by industry (e.g., "Biotechnology", "Software - Application", "Oil & Gas E&P")

minMarketCap.description: Minimum market cap in USD (e.g., 1000000000 for $1B)

maxMarketCap.description: Maximum market cap in USD (e.g., 500000000 for $500M)

sortBy.description: Sort results by field (default: filing_date). Ties are broken by filing id, so a given page is stable and reproducible for a fixed corpus.

sortOrder.description: Sort direction (default: desc). Note that paging is offset-based over a corpus that is continuously ingesting new filings, so when walking many pages of a broad date range, newly-arrived filings can shift rows between pages; page on a closed dateFrom/dateTo window if you need an exhaustive, non-overlapping traversal.

tools.name: search_sec_filings
tools.description: Search and list SEC filings by company (CIK), form type, date range, 8-K item codes and excluded forms, optionally with a full-text query over filing bodies and by company facts (market cap, float, price, sector, industry, exchange, company type, foreign issuer, recent IPO). Rows carry `id` (the internal filingId used by the filing-document and exhibit tools), cik, company_name, accession_number, form_type, filing_date, acceptedAt, primaryDocument, bodyStored and itemNumbers (plus `rank` and `snippet` with `q`); `pagination` has `total`, `totalRelation` ("eq" exact; "gte" a lower bound cut at 10,000, when `totalEstimate` is "about N"), `hasMore` and `nextCursor`. The `ciks` filter matches the filing's own CIK: a Form 4 filed under the reporting owner's CIK is not returned for the issuer's CIK. Coverage: Signal8's SEC EDGAR archive, updated through the day, in its held range (see `archiveFrom` in each response; currently from late 2021, expanding back to 2016 as the history backfill fills in). Before archiveFrom it holds only a scatter, so absence before archiveFrom is not evidence a filing was never filed; SEC EDGAR itself covers earlier periods. Record-only rows (bodyStored: false) have no stored body; the document is at its sec.gov URL. Every response carries `archiveFrom` and `rangeStartsBeforeArchive`: a range with no dateFrom or starting before archiveFrom is not definitive (`searchIndex.complete: false`, `reason: "outside_held_range"`, `heldFrom`): an empty result then means the archive holds no match from archiveFrom onward, not that no such filing exists. An empty text result is definitive only when `searchIndex.complete` is true. Full-text `q`: Query syntax: unquoted words all have to appear (any order, any distance); "quoted phrase" = exact wording; OR between alternatives (merger OR acquisition); -word or -"phrase" to exclude; w1 NEAR/10 w2 (also NEAR(10), or bare NEAR = within 10) = words close together; word* = prefix of 4+ letters (dilut* matches dilution, dilutive); $AAPL or a capitalised ticker scopes to that company; a form code (8-K, 10-Q, S-1), "item 5.02" / "8-K 1.05" and a bare year (2024) scope to that form / 8-K item / year. The archive's reading of the query is in `meta.understanding` (understand=false searches the words literally). facets=true adds `facets` per form / year / 8-K item over the whole result set (absent = not measured, never zero). sort=relevance caps page 1 per company; meta.diversity {maxPerCompany, hidden} names who has more (page with nextCursor or filter by CIK). section / exhibitTypes filters apply only when meta.sections / appliedFilters confirm them; otherwise meta.unsupported says why and the whole filing was searched. Company filters (minMarketCap … recentIpo): only issuer-filed forms are searched (third-party Form 4 / 144 / 13D/G go to `companyFilter.droppedForms` unless `companyFilter.subjectMatch` is true; with no formTypes the default is 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, S-1, S-3, DEF 14A, 20-F, 40-F, 6-K); companies with no measured value are excluded, never assumed (`companyFilter.unknown` counts them); an unknown value is a 400 listing allowed names; when the archive cannot answer, the call fails with COMPANY_FILTER_NOT_APPLIED and never returns unfiltered rows; results are cursor-paged, cannot combine with acceptedFrom/acceptedTo/bodyStored, and carry no snippet. Results are filings, not a company list or count.

ciks.description: Comma-separated CIK numbers to filter by (e.g., "320193,1018724"; zero-padded also accepted)

q.description: Full-text query over filing bodies. Query syntax: unquoted words all have to appear (any order, any distance); "quoted phrase" = exact wording; OR between alternatives (merger OR acquisition); -word or -"phrase" to exclude; w1 NEAR/10 w2 (also NEAR(10), or bare NEAR = within 10) = words close together; word* = prefix of 4+ letters (dilut* matches dilution, dilutive); $AAPL or a capitalised ticker scopes to that company; a form code (8-K, 10-Q, S-1), "item 5.02" / "8-K 1.05" and a bare year (2024) scope to that form / 8-K item / year. Example: '$AAPL "share repurchase" -"no longer"', 'cyber* NEAR/10 incident', 'item 5.02 resign*'.

sort.description: newest (by acceptance time, default) or relevance (requires q; best match first)

match.description: Word matching for q. exact = a word matches only itself ("split" does not match "splits" or "splitting"), which is EDGAR full-text search's own behaviour; stemmed = English word variations also match. Default when omitted: stemmed. The mode actually applied is in the response's meta.matchMode (with meta.matchModeFallbackReason when it differs from the one asked for); meta.engine names the search engine. Ignored without q.

facets.description: true = also return `facets`: { forms, years, items }, each a list of { value, count } over the whole result set (not just this page). Present only when the archive measured them (its OpenSearch engine); absent means not measured, not zero. Default false.

understand.description: Query understanding (default true): the archive recognises tickers/$TICKER, company names, form codes, "item N.NN" and expands synonyms, reporting what it applied in meta.understanding. false = search the words literally (also disables synonym expansion). Ignored without q.

section.description: Restricts matching to sections (comma-separated): business, risk_factors, cybersecurity, legal_proceedings, mdna, market_risk, controls (10-K/10-Q/20-F narrative items, by meaning: mdna is 10-K Item 7, 10-Q Part I Item 2 and 20-F Item 5), ex99 (press-release / EX-99.x exhibit text) and item_X_YY (the text under an 8-K item, e.g. item_5_02). Aliases: mda, risk, legal, cyber, press_release, 5.02. Unknown names are a 400. Requires q. Applied only when the response's meta.sections names it; otherwise meta.unsupported says why (e.g. the archive index does not have sections yet) and matches may come from anywhere in the filing.

exhibitTypes.description: Keeps only filings carrying any of these exhibit types (comma-separated): a family such as EX-10 (material contracts) matches every member (EX-10.1, EX-10.2…); an exact type such as EX-99.1 (usually the press release) only itself. Others: EX-97 clawback policy, EX-3 charter/bylaws, EX-4 instruments/warrants, EX-21 subsidiaries, EX-23 consents. "10.1" is accepted for EX-10.1. Listed in appliedFilters when the rows prove it; otherwise in ignoredFilters / meta.unsupported, and the rows are then unfiltered.

matchedSections.description: Per-row `matchedSections` (default true): the sections the text matched in. Absent on a row means not measured (index without sections), not "matched nowhere". Ignored without q.

cursor.description: Opaque keyset cursor from a previous response's pagination.nextCursor. Stable for deep paging while new filings arrive (page is not). Required for page 2+ of a company-filtered search.

page.description: Page number (1-indexed, default: 1). Ignored when cursor is set; not allowed with company filters.

formTypes.description: Comma-separated form types (e.g., "10-K,10-Q,8-K,S-1,S-3,424B5"). Exact match; amendments (e.g. "10-K/A") match only when listed. (With company filters, amendments are added automatically.)

excludeForms.description: Comma-separated form types to exclude (e.g., "4,13F-HR"). Exact match.

items.description: Comma-separated 8-K item codes, all required (e.g., "2.02,9.01" = results + financial statements; "5.02" = officer/director changes; "1.01" = material agreements; "3.01" = delisting notice).

dateFrom.description: Start filing date (YYYY-MM-DD). The archive only holds filings from its `archiveFrom` date (stated in every response; currently late 2021, expanding back to 2016): omitting dateFrom, or starting earlier, makes an empty result non-definitive.

minMarketCap.description: Company filter. Minimum market cap in USD (price × shares outstanding), e.g. 50000000 for $50M

maxMarketCap.description: Company filter. Maximum market cap in USD, e.g. 300000000 for under $300M

minPrice.description: Company filter. Minimum latest share price in USD

maxPrice.description: Company filter. Maximum latest share price in USD

sectors.description: Company filter. Sector names separated by "|" (or a bare comma), exact and case-sensitive (e.g. "Healthcare|Technology"). An unknown name returns a 400 listing every valid sector.

industries.description: Company filter. Industry names separated by "|", exact and case-sensitive (e.g. "Biotechnology|Airlines, Airports & Air Services"; some names contain ", ", so "|" is the safe separator; a bare comma with no space after it also separates). An unknown name returns a 400 listing every valid industry.

tools.name: get_filing_documents
tools.description: List every document in one SEC filing by accession number (the primary document, each exhibit, XML and XBRL files, graphics) with seq, type (e.g. "8-K", "EX-99.1"), description, size in bytes, `stored` and `secUrl`. Also returns the filing's cik, companyName, formType, filingDate, acceptedAt, bodyStored, primaryDocument, indexUrl, and `filingId`. A document with an `exhibitId` has readable stored text under that exhibit id; `filingId` identifies the whole submission text. `exhibitId: null` means the document has no readable text row here (XML/XBRL/graphics, or text not held); its `secUrl` still opens it. When `readableIdsResolved` is false the id lookup failed and exhibitId is omitted (unknown, not "none"). `stored: false` means Signal8 holds the filing record but not that document's body; it exists on EDGAR at `secUrl`. A filing not held in the archive returns a not-found error; its documents are still on EDGAR. Coverage: Signal8's SEC EDGAR archive, updated through the day, in its held range (see `archiveFrom` in each response; currently from late 2021, expanding back to 2016 as the history backfill fills in). Before archiveFrom it holds only a scatter, so absence before archiveFrom is not evidence a filing was never filed; SEC EDGAR itself covers earlier periods. Record-only rows (bodyStored: false) have no stored body; the document is at its sec.gov URL.

accessionNumber.description: SEC accession number, dashed ("0001193125-22-010026") or 18-digit compact form

tools.name: get_filing_structured
tools.description: Parsed, machine-readable data from an ownership or holdings filing, by accession number. `kind`: "ownership" (Form 3/4/5 and amendments): issuer, reporting owners with relationship (director, officer title, 10% owner, or the filer's own "Other" text) and `parsed.transactions` (per transaction: table nonDerivative/derivative, securityTitle, transactionDate, code, acquiredDisposed A/D, shares, pricePerShare, sharesOwnedAfter, ownership D/I; derivatives add exercisePrice, exerciseDate, expirationDate, underlyingTitle, underlyingShares); "thirteen_f" (13F-HR): period, holdings with cusip, issuer, shares/principal, put/call, discretion and voting; "schedule13" (XML SCHEDULE 13D/G, 2025 onward): reporting persons, percent of class, items. 13F VALUES: `valueThousands` is the raw filed number, whose unit changed from thousands to whole dollars for filings on/after 2023-01-03; `valueUsd` / `totalMarketValueUsd` are normalised to dollars (null when the unit cannot be determined) and `valueUnit` names the unit. Holdings are capped at holdingsLimit (default 200); `holdingsTotal` is the full count, `holdingsTruncated` says whether rows were cut. A null value means not stated in the filing; it does not mean zero (a gift with no price has pricePerShare null; `directShares` is null on a derivative-only Form 4). `parsed.transactions` absent (not empty) means the table could not be read; totals still apply. `parsed: null` on a 13F means no information table (e.g. 13F-NT), not zero holdings. Unsupported forms, pre-2025 Schedule 13D/G and filings not in the archive return a not-found error with `details.reason`; their raw text remains readable as a filing document. Coverage: Signal8's SEC EDGAR archive, updated through the day, in its held range (see `archiveFrom` in each response; currently from late 2021, expanding back to 2016 as the history backfill fills in). Before archiveFrom it holds only a scatter, so absence before archiveFrom is not evidence a filing was never filed; SEC EDGAR itself covers earlier periods. Record-only rows (bodyStored: false) have no stored body; the document is at its sec.gov URL.

accessionNumber.description: SEC accession number of a Form 3/4/5, 13F-HR or SCHEDULE 13D/G, dashed or 18-digit compact form

holdingsLimit.description: 13F only: max holdings rows to return (default 200, max 5000)

tools.name: get_filing_document
tools.description: Get the full raw text/HTML content of an SEC filing by its internal filing ID (the `id` on filing search rows, or `filingId` from an accession-number lookup or a filing's document list). Returns the complete filing document, which can be very large (10-K filings can be 1MB+); maxLength truncates content for previews. The response includes company_name, form_type, filing_date, cik, and accession_number alongside the content. Record-only filings (bodyStored: false) have no body here; the document is on sec.gov. Content is the whole submission as filed. Coverage: Signal8's SEC EDGAR archive, updated through the day, in its held range (see `archiveFrom` in each response; currently from late 2021, expanding back to 2016 as the history backfill fills in). Before archiveFrom it holds only a scatter, so absence before archiveFrom is not evidence a filing was never filed; SEC EDGAR itself covers earlier periods. Record-only rows (bodyStored: false) have no stored body; the document is at its sec.gov URL.

filingId.description: Internal filing ID (numeric), the `id` on filing search rows.

maxLength.description: Truncate content to this many characters. Useful for previewing large filings. Response includes a "truncated" boolean when truncation is applied.

tools.name: get_filing_exhibits
tools.description: List the readable exhibits (individual documents with stored text) within an SEC filing, by internal filing ID. Returns each exhibit's `id` (the exhibit id for reading that exhibit's text), exhibit type, description, content size and sec_url. Excludes XML/XBRL and documents with no stored text.

filingId.description: Internal filing ID (numeric), the `id` on filing search rows.

tools.name: get_exhibit_content
tools.description: Get the full text/HTML content of a single exhibit from an SEC filing, by exhibit id. Returns the exhibit text along with exhibit_type, description, company_name, accession_number, and form_type. maxLength truncates large exhibits. Exhibit ids appear as `exhibitId` in a filing's document list, as `id` in a filing's exhibit list, and as `exhibit_id` on full-text search matches.

id.description: Exhibit ID (numeric), as listed for the filing's exhibits.

maxLength.description: Truncate content to this many characters. Response includes a "truncated" boolean.

tools.name: search_filing_text
tools.description: Full-text search across SEC filing content that returns the matching passage: one match per filing, with the exhibit it was found in (`exhibit_id`, `exhibit_type`) and a snippet with context. Query syntax: unquoted words all have to appear (any order, any distance); "quoted phrase" = exact wording; OR between alternatives (merger OR acquisition); -word or -"phrase" to exclude; w1 NEAR/10 w2 (also NEAR(10), or bare NEAR = within 10) = words close together; word* = prefix of 4+ letters (dilut* matches dilution, dilutive); $AAPL or a capitalised ticker scopes to that company; a form code (8-K, 10-Q, S-1), "item 5.02" / "8-K 1.05" and a bare year (2024) scope to that form / 8-K item / year. Quoted multi-word phrases match as phrases; the archive's reading of the query is in meta.understanding. Suited to locating specific clauses ("change of control", "anti-dilution", "right of first refusal") and to the excerpt of a known filing (accessionNumber or filingId). It has no filing-level paging, totals, date ranges, 8-K item, excluded-form or company filters. Filters: CIK, filing, accession number, form type, section (risk_factors, mdna, ex99 …; applied only when meta.sections confirms it, otherwise meta.unsupported says the whole filing was searched) and exhibitTypes (EX-10 …). Coverage: Signal8's SEC EDGAR archive, updated through the day, in its held range (see `archiveFrom` in each response; currently from late 2021, expanding back to 2016 as the history backfill fills in). Before archiveFrom it holds only a scatter, so absence before archiveFrom is not evidence a filing was never filed; SEC EDGAR itself covers earlier periods. Record-only rows (bodyStored: false) have no stored body; the document is at its sec.gov URL.

pattern.description: Search query (minimum 2 characters): "exact phrase", OR, -exclude, w1 NEAR/n w2, word*, $TICKER. A CIK/filing-scoped search whose text is not indexed yet falls back to a literal case-insensitive substring match (response engine: "substring"); there each "quoted phrase" and bare word must appear (quotes stripped), and meta.substringTerms lists the terms matched. OR, NEAR, -exclude and word* are not applied on that path.

cik.description: Filter to a specific company by CIK number

filingId.description: Filter to a specific filing by internal ID

accessionNumber.description: Filter to a specific filing by SEC accession number

snippetLength.description: Characters of context around each match (default: 200)

sort.description: Result order: newest (default) or relevance (best match first)

match.description: Word matching. exact = a word matches only itself ("split" does not match "splits"), which is EDGAR full-text search's behaviour; stemmed = English word variations also match. Default when omitted: stemmed. The mode actually applied is reported in the response's meta.matchMode.

understand.description: Query understanding (default true): tickers/$TICKER, company names, form codes, "item N.NN" and synonym expansion, reported in meta.understanding. false = match the words literally.

facets.description: true = also return `facets` { forms, years, items }: [{ value, count }] over the whole match set. Absent when not measured (not zero). Default false.

section.description: Restricts matching to sections (comma-separated): business, risk_factors, cybersecurity, legal_proceedings, mdna, market_risk, controls (10-K/10-Q/20-F narrative items, by meaning: mdna is 10-K Item 7, 10-Q Part I Item 2 and 20-F Item 5), ex99 (press-release / EX-99.x exhibit text) and item_X_YY (the text under an 8-K item, e.g. item_5_02). Aliases: mda, risk, legal, cyber, press_release, 5.02. Unknown names are a 400. Requires q. Applied only when the response's meta.sections names it; otherwise meta.unsupported says why (e.g. the archive index does not have sections yet) and matches may come from anywhere in the filing.

exhibitTypes.description: Keeps only filings carrying any of these exhibit types (comma-separated): a family such as EX-10 (material contracts) matches every member (EX-10.1, EX-10.2…); an exact type such as EX-99.1 (usually the press release) only itself. Others: EX-97 clawback policy, EX-3 charter/bylaws, EX-4 instruments/warrants, EX-21 subsidiaries, EX-23 consents. "10.1" is accepted for EX-10.1. Listed in appliedFilters when the rows prove it; otherwise in ignoredFilters / meta.unsupported, and the rows are then unfiltered.

matchedSections.description: Per-row `matchedSections` (default true): the sections the text matched in. Absent on a row means not measured (index without sections), not "matched nowhere".

tools.name: lookup_accession_number
tools.description: Look up a filing or exhibit by its SEC accession number. Supports both dashed format (e.g., "0001193125-22-010026") and compact 18-digit format. Returns filing metadata including company name, form type, filing date, exhibit count and `filingId` (the internal id of the stored filing). If the filing is held in Signal8's archive (isInDatabase: true) its content is readable through that filingId; if it is only found on SEC EDGAR the response has isInDatabase: false and basic metadata only.

accessionNumber.description: SEC accession number in dashed (e.g., "0001193125-22-010026") or compact 18-digit format

tools.name: screen_sec_filings_performance
tools.description: Analyze stock price performance after SEC filings. Returns individual filing records with pre-computed price returns at +1 day, +3 days, +7 days, and +30 days after the filing date (numbers in percent points: 4.35 = +4.35%; null = not measured), plus aggregate statistics (average, median, % negative, best, worst) across all matching filings. Company-level filters (sector, industry, market cap, exchange) combine with filing filters (form type, date range). Answers questions like "how did biotech stocks perform after S-1 filings?" or "what was the average 7-day return after 8-K filings from companies under $500M market cap?". These are past returns, not a forecast.

tools.name: get_insiders
tools.description: Get insider trading discovery data for a company. Includes cluster buying detection, entity-centric insider model, and Form 4 cross-referencing. Shows insider transactions with buying/selling patterns that may signal upcoming corporate actions. Each insider includes a transactionBreakdown by SEC code (P=Purchase, S=Sale, F=Tax withholding, M=Exercise, G=Gift, A=Award), netSharesSold12m (code S only, excludes tax withholding), and isPrimarilyTaxWithholding flag to distinguish routine RSU vesting from discretionary selling. Supports pagination with limit/offset.

tools.name: get_ownership
tools.description: Get the unified ownership breakdown for a company, combining Form 4 insider holdings, 13F institutional holdings and 13D/13G activist positions, resolved across the three form types into one view. allHolders is paginated via limit/offset (default 100); aggregate stats (institutional / insider / beneficial totals and percentages, plus `retail`) are always complete. `sharesOutstanding`, the denominator of every percentage, is dated by `sharesOutstandingAsOf` + `sharesOutstandingAsOfKind` ("stated" = issuer's statement date; "checked" = last confirmed against a vendor; "none" = date not recorded) and `sharesOutstandingSource`; a count is only meaningful with its date. `retail` is the unattributed residual (shares no filing accounts for, including recent offering buyers and non-filing holders): an upper bound on retail, not a retail count; withheld (null) with `retail.reason: "filed_exceeds_outstanding"` when counted filings exceed shares outstanding. A bucket whose shares exceed shares outstanding by more than a 2% timing tolerance has `percentOfOutstanding` withheld (null, `percentWithheldReason: "ownership_exceeds_outstanding"`) with `totalShares` still published (e.g. another share basis such as ordinary shares vs ADSs, another class, lent shares reported twice, filings predating a buyback); the shares and the reason are the measurement, and the withheld percent is not 100%, 0% or any other percent. In that case `retail.reason` is `ownership_exceeds_outstanding` and `filedSumPercent` is absent. A null percent with no `percentWithheldReason` means no share count was available. `beneficial.staleShares` / `stalePercentOfOutstanding` / `staleHolderCount` is a measured subset of the counted 5%+ total resting on 13D/G schedules >= 24 months old with no newer reaffirming filing by the holder family: not a deduction. `reaffirmedBy` names the newer filing; `staleFiling.ageMonths` marks a row with none. `stalePercentOfOutstanding: null` is not measurable, not zero.

limit.description: Maximum holders to return in allHolders (default: 100, max: 100)

tools.name: get_institutions
tools.description: Get institutional holders (13F filers) for a company. Returns institutions that hold positions in this stock based on SEC 13F filings, including shares held, portfolio weight, and filing dates. Useful for understanding institutional ownership concentration.

tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific institutional investor by their SEC CIK number. Returns the institution name, total AUM, number of holdings, and filing history. Takes the institution's CIK.

cik.description: SEC CIK number of the institution (e.g., "0001067983" for Berkshire Hathaway)

tools.name: get_institution_holdings
tools.description: Get the full portfolio holdings for a specific institution by CIK. Returns all positions from their latest 13F filing with shares, value, and portfolio weight. Supports pagination for institutions with large portfolios.

cik.description: SEC CIK number of the institution

tools.description: Diff two quarterly 13F snapshots for an institution. Compares the latest filing against the prior quarter and returns per-position changes: new positions, increased, decreased, and exited. Sorted by |changePercent| descending so the biggest moves surface first. The diff is computed server-side in a single query.

cik.description: SEC CIK number of the institution (e.g., "0001067983" for Berkshire Hathaway)

tools.name: get_institution_activity
tools.description: Get an institution's position changes over recent 13F periods by CIK. Reads the number of trailing periods to include.

cik.description: SEC CIK number of the institution

periods.description: Number of trailing quarters to include (default: 4, max: 12)

tools.name: get_institution_filings
tools.description: Get the list of 13F filings for an institution by CIK, with pagination.

cik.description: SEC CIK number of the institution

tools.name: get_institution_derivatives
tools.description: Get an institution's reported put/call derivative positions by CIK (13F options), with pagination and sorting.

cik.description: SEC CIK number of the institution

tools.name: get_institution_portfolio_analytics
tools.description: Get sector allocation and top holdings analytics for an institution's portfolio by CIK.

cik.description: SEC CIK number of the institution

tools.name: get_institutions_leaderboards
tools.description: Two market-wide institution leaderboards in one call: topByAum (largest holders by assets under management, name-deduped) and mostActive (highest 13F position-change volume). No CIK required. Each section is capped by `limit`; it is not the full paginated AUM list.

tools.name: get_insider_transactions
tools.description: Get detailed insider transaction history for a company from Form 4 filings. Returns individual buy/sell transactions with insider name, title, shares, price, and transaction codes. Supports pagination for companies with extensive insider activity. Optional year/month and transactionCode filters (purchases P, sales S, etc.) narrow results. Each row's sharesOwnedFollowing is the holding on that row's ownership line only (securityTitle + directOrIndirect + natureOfOwnership), not the insider's total position; insiders often report several lines, so one row is not a basis for a "% of position" figure. holdingsByInsider lists every line with its as-of filing; its sumOfReportedLines is not beneficial ownership (lines can be stale). A trade re-reported in a later filing is listed once.

month.description: Filter by transaction month (1-12, requires year)

transactionCode.description: Filter by SEC transaction code: P=Purchase, S=Sale, A=Grant/Award, M=Exercise/Conversion, F=Tax withholding, G=Gift, C=Conversion, W=Will, D=Disposition to issuer, etc.

tools.name: get_insider_cluster_buys
tools.description: Detect cluster buying for a company: periods where 3+ distinct insiders bought shares (Form 4 open-market purchases, code P) within a 14-day window, over a lookback of 7, 30 or 90 days (default 90). Returns clusterBuyingDetected, the strongest clusterWindow, a summary (totalValue is null when no purchase disclosed a price, and is a floor when unpricedPurchaseCount > 0) and the deduped purchases. `asOf` and `lookback` state the date range covered; clusterBuyingDetected false means none in that range only.

days.description: Lookback in days by transaction date: 7, 30 or 90 (default 90)

tools.name: get_institution_top_aum
tools.description: Discover top institutional holders across the entire company universe ranked by assets under management (AUM), across all companies rather than for a single company. Optionally set a minimum AUM. Useful for identifying smart money flows and major institutional positioning trends.

minAum.description: Minimum AUM in USD to filter institutions (e.g., 1000000000 for $1B+)

tools.name: search_institutions
tools.description: Search institutional investors (13F filers) by name. Returns matching institutions with CIK, name, AUM, holdings count, and latest filing period. Matches part of a fund or investment manager name (e.g., "Vanguard", "BlackRock", "Citadel"). Results are ranked by AUM descending.

tools.name: get_insider_cross_company
tools.description: Discover insider trading patterns across multiple companies (the whole universe, not a single ticker): insiders active across multiple companies, cluster buying patterns, and large transactions. Optional filters: insider name, transaction type, or date range. Cluster buying is computed only for purchases (transactionType P, the default). Useful for detecting coordinated insider activity, cross-company insider networks, and market-wide buying/selling trends.

insiderName.description: Filter by insider name (partial match, e.g., "Musk" or "Cohen")

startDate.description: Start date, YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., "2025-01-01"); a full ISO timestamp is cut to its date. Either bound may be given alone. An unparseable date is rejected, never ignored.

endDate.description: End date, YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., "2025-12-31"); a full ISO timestamp is cut to its date.

tools.name: get_compliance
tools.description: Get full compliance rules evaluation for a company: Nasdaq/NYSE deficiency detection, bid price tracking, and delinquent filing detection, combining SEC filing data, market data and exchange rules. Rules cover bid price, equity, reverse-split limit, market value of publicly held shares, publicly held shares, holders, timely periodic filings, annual meeting and audit committee, per exchange tier. Standards that could not be judged from any measurement are listed in `notEvaluated`: they are neither passing nor failing. Neither a `notEvaluated` standard nor the absence of a deficiency notice is evidence of compliance.

tools.name: screen_companies
tools.description: Screen companies by price range, volume, cash runway, float, shares outstanding, market cap, industry, listing exchange (NASDAQ/NYSE/AMEX), listing market (market="otc" / "exchange"; the reliable OTC test, as the exchange label is inconsistent on OTC rows), float data source, TTM dividend yield and snapshot cash (minCash / maxCash). Sortable by any sortable column. Returns matching companies with key metrics and pagination. Float: "float" is the measured point float (null on a withheld dilution-snapshot row, which then carries "floatEstimate" + "floatEstimateBound" ("point" / "ceiling" / "floor") + "floatEstimateBasis"). A point estimate is a number with its basis as the caveat; a ceiling or floor is a bound, not a figure: the float is not stated and is at most (ceiling) or at least (floor) that number. floatEstimate is not a basis for a market cap, percent-of-float or short-interest ratio. minFloat / maxFloat and the computed_float sort use the figure's value, so a bounded row is kept; a row with neither is not measured, not 0. `shares_outstanding` is dated by `sharesOutstandingAsOf` + `sharesOutstandingAsOfKind` (stated / checked / none = date not recorded) and `sharesOutstandingSource`; the count is only meaningful with its date. Cash runway: a null cash_runway_months carries cashRunwayReason. "estimate_would_be_negative" = the last cash figure (dated cashRunwayAsOf) rolled forward by burn is below zero: estimated exhausted, not a reported zero balance; maxCashRunway drops such rows unless includeRunwayExhausted=true. Any other or null reason is not a runway claim. estimatedCurrentCash (estimatedCashAsOf) is the snapshot's USD cash projection, only for snapshot-covered companies: null = not measured, not "no cash"; a non-USD filer has it null and is never matched by minCash / maxCash. dividendYield (TTM cash dividends with an ex-date in the last 365 days / current price, %), nextExDate, lastExDate: null = not measured or not a payer, not 0%. listingMarket: "exchange" / "otc", null = unknown. Each row carries live trading-halt status (halted/haltCode/haltedAt; false/null when trading normally); excludeHalted=true drops currently-halted tickers.

country.description: Company universe by issuer domicile: "US" (default), "CA" (Canadian companies via their US-OTC/US cross-listings), or "all"

industry.description: Filter by company industry (exact match, e.g. "Biotechnology", "Software")

exchange.description: Filter by listing exchange: NASDAQ (every tier), NYSE (includes NYSE Arca), or AMEX (NYSE American). Each matches every spelling of that exchange; names that moved to OTC never match. For OTC use market="otc" instead

market.description: Listing market: "otc" (OTC Markets) or "exchange" (NASDAQ / NYSE / NYSE American / Arca / Cboe). Companies with no listing record match neither

minCashRunway.description: Minimum estimated months of cash remaining

maxCashRunway.description: Maximum estimated months of cash remaining

includeRunwayExhausted.description: When true, maxCashRunway also returns companies whose estimated cash is already exhausted (cash_runway_months null, cashRunwayReason "estimate_would_be_negative"); they sort first on an ascending runway sort. Default false

minCash.description: Minimum dilution-snapshot cash projection in USD (estimatedCurrentCash). Snapshot-covered companies reporting in USD only

maxCash.description: Maximum dilution-snapshot cash projection in USD (estimatedCurrentCash). Snapshot-covered companies only; an uncovered company is not measured, not excluded for having cash

minSharesOutstanding.description: Minimum shares outstanding from SEC EDGAR

maxSharesOutstanding.description: Maximum shares outstanding from SEC EDGAR

minMarketCapComputed.description: Minimum market cap in USD (price * shares outstanding)

maxMarketCapComputed.description: Maximum market cap in USD (price * shares outstanding)

minDividendYield.description: Minimum TTM dividend yield in percent (e.g. 3 for 3%). Rows with no measured yield never match.

maxDividendYield.description: Maximum TTM dividend yield in percent. Rows with no measured yield never match.

sortBy.description: Column to sort results by (default: volume)

excludeHalted.description: When true, exclude tickers with a currently-active trading halt (regulatory or volatility) from the results. Default false: halted rows are included and carry halted/haltCode/haltedAt fields.

tools.name: get_premarket_scan_history
tools.description: Historical market-wide premarket scan for one past ET trade date: every ticker with that day's premarket (default) session volume and its RVOL vs the trailing 30-day same-session baseline (the same per-ticker RVOL math, across the market for one date). Filters on RVOL, market cap, price and float support backtesting screens like "sub-$500M tickers with premarket RVOL > 5 on 2026-07-20"; rows ranked by RVOL descending. A future or non-trading date returns an empty list with a reason (not an error). Each row reports "baselineState" (why its RVOL is or is not null), "advRatio" (volume / trailing 30-session average full-day volume), "advDays", and the RVOL denominator "baselineVolume" with "baselineThin" (true under 200 shares): a 90x RVOL off a 1-share baseline is arithmetically correct and analytically meaningless, mostly an early-asOfTime effect on liquid large caps; minBaselineVolume / minSessionVolume exclude such rows. includeNoHistory=true surfaces high-volume tickers with no computable RVOL (e.g. first-session listings). meta reports asOfApplied / asOfIgnored / asOfIgnoredReason, so an unhonoured time-of-day request is visible. Tickers with no screener value for a price / market-cap / float filter (just renamed or listed) are not silently dropped: "meta.unscreened" reports their count, filter families and tickers, and includeUnscreened=true returns them tagged "unscreenedFilters"; that tag means the filter was not measured for the ticker, not that it is out of range.

date.description: Required past ET trade date to scan (YYYY-MM-DD). Future/non-trade dates return an empty list.

session.description: Session bucket to scan (default premarket). "all" = full extended day.

minRvol.description: Minimum RVOL (day session volume ÷ trailing 30-day baseline). Drops rows whose baseline is not yet warm.

includeNoHistory.description: Also return the cohort minRvol structurally hides: tickers with NO computable RVOL. Two kinds, told apart by each row's "baselineState": "no-history" (a new listing with no prior trading history at all, so RVOL is meaningless rather than merely missing; e.g. a stock that printed 20M shares on its first-ever session) and "no-cutoff-history" (an established ticker that simply never traded at this cutoff before, a genuine wake-up). Both come back with rvol=null and are always ranked below every real-RVOL row, ordered among themselves by "advRatio". "advRatio" (volume / trailing 30-session average full-day volume, null when no full-day denominator exists) and "advDays" (its sample size) size them; advRatio is not an RVOL and is not comparable to one. Inert unless minRvol is set. Default false.

minMarketCap.description: Minimum market cap in USD (market_cap_computed = price × shares outstanding).

maxMarketCap.description: Maximum market cap in USD (e.g. 500000000 for sub-$500M).

minBaselineVolume.description: Minimum RVOL DENOMINATOR in shares. Drops rows whose "baselineVolume" is below it, plus every row that has no baseline at all. This is the direct fix for a huge RVOL computed against a near-zero baseline (e.g. 102 shares ÷ a 1.2-share baseline = 87x on a $10B company that just does not trade at 04:30). 200 matches the "baselineThin" flag; higher is stricter. It changes no RVOL; it only removes rows. It also excludes the includeNoHistory cohort, which by definition has no denominator.

minSessionVolume.description: Minimum RVOL numerator in shares: the scanned session's own volume. It measures whether enough actually traded, where minBaselineVolume measures whether the comparison is meaningful at all; neither subsumes the other (a 1,000-share floor here cuts thin-baseline rows from ~26% to ~3%, yet a name with an 860-share baseline and 11.8M shares traded passes this and fails a baseline floor).

includeUnscreened.description: Also return rows that could not be RATED against the price / market-cap / float bounds above, because company_screener_data holds no value for them (typically a symbol renamed or listed within the last day; the source is a vendor screener that lags a rename by ~a day). Each such row carries "unscreenedFilters" naming the families that could not be applied, and the matching value field is null. That means not measured, neither "matched" nor "did not match". Default false, in which case those rows are excluded from "rows" but are still reported in meta.unscreened (count / columns / tickers), so they are never silently dropped. Inert unless a price, market-cap or float filter is supplied.

limit.description: Max rows to return (1–200, default 50). Rows are ranked by RVOL desc.

asOfTime.description: Optional true time-of-day premarket basis. Any HH:MM ET premarket time; snapped to the nearest 15-minute grid cutoff (04:00–09:15, ties resolve to the earlier cutoff). When set, RVOL is cumulative premarket volume known BY that cutoff ÷ the trailing baselineDays (default 30) average of the same cutoff: a real time-of-day comparison, not the full 04:00–09:30 session. Each returned row carries a "basis" field: "asof-0700" (the snapped cutoff actually used) when a precomputed row exists, else "full-session" (automatic per-row fallback; the as-of series is forward-looking and may be sparse). Only applies to a premarket scan. Unset means full-session premarket volume. "meta.asOfApplied" is the snapped cutoff actually used, or null, and "meta.asOfIgnored" / "meta.asOfIgnoredReason" explain a fallback ("date-not-covered": the as-of grid has not been computed for this date, so the numbers are full-session; "non-premarket-session": asOfTime only applies to a premarket scan; "unparseable"). Coverage is a set with holes that grows as the backfill runs, so there is no single cutover date; the meta is per request. An unhonoured asOfTime is never an error, so the meta is the only reliable signal. This basis is where near-zero RVOL baselines come from (see "baselineThin" and minBaselineVolume).

baselineDays.description: Rolling RVOL baseline window, in trading rows (same-session days). Default 30; values outside 20-250 are clamped. This is the DENOMINATOR window: every RVOL in the response is that period's volume divided by the average of the trailing N same-session (or same-cutoff) days, excluding the day itself. A SHORTER window tracks recent regime changes faster and is noisier; a LONGER one is smoother and slower to react. The warm-up lookback scales with it automatically, so a wide window is never under-filled into an inflated ratio; the minimum-warm-days gate (20 prior sessions) does NOT scale down, so at the 30-row default a ticker needs 20 of its last 30 sessions populated before rvol is non-null. Unset means the standard 30-day baseline; 90 reproduces the pre-2026-09 window.

tools.name: get_split_history
tools.description: Get stock split history for a company including forward and reverse splits with dates, ratios, type classification, and cumulative 2-year reverse split ratio. Relevant for Nasdaq/NYSE minimum bid-price compliance (1:250 cumulative reverse-split cap). A null `cumulativeReverseSplitRatio2yr` means the cumulative cannot be stated, which is not the same as no reverse splits; `cumulativeWithheldReason` distinguishes the two. `unconfirmed_splits_in_window` means at least one in-window reverse split is evidenced by only one source, so no cumulative is defensible: the confirmed splits alone would understate it, and understating a cumulative can put an issuer that breaches the 1:250 cap under it. Each row also carries `confirmed`; a `confirmed: false` split appears only in the announcement calendar, which retains every announcement and retracts none, so it is usually an amended or superseded announcement and occasionally a real split the effected-splits ledger missed. Both are returned. `ratioDisplay` and `type` are likewise null for a ratio whose exact factor cannot be determined. Not every vendor "split" is a split: stock dividends and other distributions under 25%, spin-off price factors and consolidations under 1.5x are returned in `nonSplitAdjustments` (each with a `kind` and `meaning`), not in `splits`, and are excluded from `totalSplits`, `reverseSplitCount` and the cumulative. They are not splits.

tools.name: get_split_performance
tools.description: Get how one ticker's price moved in the N calendar days after each stock split it already executed (forward or reverse), newest first, up to 30 splits, in one call. Past executed splits only: upcoming, approved or pending splits are not included. Each split row carries executionDate, ratio ("1-for-12" = 12 old shares became 1), kind (reverse | forward | other), lastPreSplitDate, firstPostSplitDate, firstPostSplitCloseAsTraded, windowEndDate, windowEndCloseAsTraded, sessionsInWindow, changeFromFirstPostSplitClosePct (first post-split close to the last close in the window), changeFromLastPreSplitClosePct (the last pre-split close moved onto the post-split basis by the split ratio, so the split itself is not counted as a move), lowestLowVsFirstClosePct and highestHighVsFirstClosePct. Basis: the response field basis states it. Each row is on that split's own post-split basis (daily bars as traded); prices are not adjusted onto today's basis, so % moves are comparable across rows and prices are not. A null value means not measured; it does not mean 0 or "no move". Causes: a missing bar, a bar print Signal8 refused as implausible, or a window that reaches a later split (anotherSplitInWindow: true, its % withheld). notMeasured on a row names the reason per null field; dataGap = no daily bar within 7 days after the split. Stock dividends, spin-off price factors and consolidations under 1.5x that the vendor files as splits are not splits: they are listed in nonSplitAdjustments (kind, meaning), never measured or counted, and a split window containing one has its % withheld (nonSplitAdjustmentInWindow: true). An empty splits array means no executed split is on record in Signal8 split history, which is not evidence that none occurred. splitsMeasured and fellInWindow count only measured rows. asOf is the latest window-end bar date. These are past price moves, not a forecast and not investment advice. Included in Signal8 Pro: an HTTP 403 FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE means the API key's account is not on Pro, and the response then carries no price data for the company.

windowDays.description: Calendar days after each split to measure, 1 to 365 (default 30).

limit.description: Most recent executed splits to measure, 1 to 30 (default 20).

annotations.title: Get Price Performance After Each Split

Each data type is cached independently. Specify which types to include or omit to get above-the-fold defaults (profile, stock-summary, holdings, sectors).
