include.description: Comma-separated list of data types to include. Available: profile,holdings,sectors,countries,stock-summary,performance,news,analyst,comparables. Default (when omitted): profile,stock-summary,holdings,sectors

tools.name: get_politicians
tools.description: List and search congressional politicians who have STOCK Act trading disclosures. Filter by party (D/R/I), state, or search by name. Returns paginated results with trade counts, last trade date, and net buy/sell direction over the trailing 12 months.

state.description: Filter by US state (2-letter code, e.g. "CA", "TX")

tools.name: get_politician_detail
tools.description: Get the full profile for a politician including party, state, chamber, trade statistics, filing delay metrics, most traded sector, and their 10 most recent transactions. The politician is identified by URL slug (e.g. "sen-nancy-pelosi").

tools.name: get_politician_transactions
tools.description: Get paginated trade history for a specific politician. Returns individual STOCK Act disclosures with ticker, transaction type, amount range, filing delay, and late filing flag. Includes a summary with total buys/sells and net value.

tools.name: get_politician_activity
tools.description: Get activity metrics for a politician broken down by period (30d, 90d, 1y, all-time). Includes buy/sell counts and values per period, most traded tickers (top 10), and transaction type breakdown. Useful for analyzing trading patterns over time.

tools.name: get_politicians_most_active
tools.description: Discover the most active congressional traders ranked by trade count within a lookback period. Returns each politician with trade count, tickers traded, buy/sell values, and top tickers. Useful for identifying the most prolific political traders.

tools.name: get_politician_recent_trades
tools.description: Get recent STOCK Act trades across all politicians. Each trade includes the senator info, ticker, transaction type, amount, and filing delay. Filter by direction (buy/sell) and lookback period. Useful for monitoring current congressional trading activity.

tools.name: get_politician_disclosures
tools.description: Per-disclosure feed of politician trades: one item per congressional STOCK Act periodic transaction report (PTR) or executive-branch OGE Form 278-T that contains at least one trade whose bracket lower bound is >= minAmount. Each item carries the politician, filing link, filing delay, and every trade of the report sorted largest bracket first, with qualifyingTradeCount for how many clear the threshold. Polling contract: the returned nextCursor, sent back as `since`, returns each disclosure exactly once (for the same minAmount and kinds); nextCursor is returned even when items is empty, and hasMore true means more items are immediately available. Without `since` only disclosures that became complete in the last 48h are returned. A report is emitted only after no new row of it has arrived for a settle window (~8h), so items lag the filing by hours; a report that grows materially afterwards (+25 trades or +20%) is emitted once more with a higher `revision`, and `replacesPrevious: true` marks a report previously delivered under the same `id`. filingDelayDays (longest lag), isLateFiling (>45 days) and lateTradeCount exclude trades with transactionDateSuspect=true: a date lagging its own otherwise on-time report by about one year is a probable mistyped year upstream, listed as filed and counted in suspectDateCount, and its lag is not a measured filing delay. owner null means the filing did not state an owner ("Not stated"); it does not mean "Self". amountRange is the filed bracket; amountMin null means the bracket was not parsed (not $0), amountMax null means "Over $50,000,000" or unparsed, and ticker null means a non-equity asset.

since.description: Opaque cursor: the nextCursor from a previous call, verbatim. Omit only on the first call.

minAmount.description: USD threshold compared to each trade's bracket lower bound (default: 50001). A disclosure qualifies when ANY of its trades meets it.

kinds.description: Which disclosure kinds to include (default: both). 'congressional' = STOCK Act PTRs (Senate + House), 'executive' = OGE 278-T (Cabinet-level officials).

tools.name: get_politician_late_filers
tools.description: Get STOCK Act late filings: trades whose disclosure was filed more than 45 days after the transaction, the latest the STOCK Act allows. Lateness is a fact about the dates on the report, not a finding of illegality or a violation: an extension, an amendment or a late notice of the trade can each explain a long gap. Sorted by filing delay descending. Excludes trades whose transaction date is suspect (a probable mistyped year upstream, about one year off the rest of its own on-time filing); their delay is not measured. owner null means not stated; it does not mean "Self".

tools.name: get_politician_committees
tools.description: Get committee assignments for a politician including committee name, chamber, role (Chair, Ranking Member, etc.), and subcommittee memberships, for relating trading activity to committee oversight areas. The politician is identified by URL slug (e.g. "sen-nancy-pelosi").

tools.name: get_politician_votes
tools.description: Get voting records for a politician by slug. Returns congressional votes with bill info, position (Yea/Nay/Not Voting), and result. Useful for assessing alignment between a politician's votes and their trading positions. Requires Bioguide ID resolution.

tools.name: get_politician_pnl
tools.description: Get estimated realized + unrealized profit & loss for a politician. Methodology: each disclosed trade amount range is converted to an estimated share count using the stock's historical market price on the transaction date, then FIFO-matched on shares (realized = (sellPrice - buyPrice) x matched shares); open positions are marked to the current price for unrealized P&L. Covers Congress (sen-/rep-) and executive branch (exec-) officials, identified by URL slug. Response includes a `totals` object (estimatedRealizedPnl, estimatedUnrealizedPnl, winRate, realizedTrades, tickersTraded) and a `byTicker[]` breakdown (estimatedShares, avgCostBasis, currentPrice, realizedPnl, unrealizedPnl, unrealizedPnlPercent); byTicker open positions double as the estimated holdings. All figures are estimates (±25-40% from disclosure bracket width).

slug.description: Politician URL slug: congressional ("sen-nancy-pelosi", "rep-...") or executive ("exec-trump-donald-j")

tools.name: get_politicians_pnl_leaderboard
tools.description: Rank politicians (Congress + executive branch) by estimated trading P&L across the universe. Sort by total P&L, win rate, or traded volume. P&L uses price-adjusted share estimation: disclosed amount ranges → estimated shares via historical price → FIFO on shares → open positions marked to current price. Figures are ESTIMATES (±25-40% from disclosure bracket width).

tools.name: get_politician_scorecard
tools.description: Top 5 and bottom 5 politicians (Congress + executive-branch officials) by estimated trading P&L over a trailing window (default and only supported window: 90 days), plus SPY's return over the same window as a benchmark, and imageUrl: a 2160x2700 PNG card of the same ranking (null when unavailable; card.reason says why). All P&L figures are estimates (estimate: true, estimateRange "±25–40%"): disclosed amount ranges are converted to shares at the historical close, FIFO-matched, and open positions marked to the latest quote. The card prints "Estimates from disclosed amount ranges (±25–40%). Not investment advice." The `metric` field defines the figure: P&L on trades disclosed inside the window only, i.e. realized on round trips opened and closed in the window plus unrealized on positions opened in the window. It is not lifetime P&L; sales of positions bought before the window are not counted. Eligibility: at least 5 trades in the window (eligibility.minTradesInWindow), so a single lucky trade cannot top the board. Each row: slug, fullTitle ("Senator", "Representative", or an executive official's filed title), fullName, displayName, party and state as full words (the publishable form, rather than "Sen." or "D-CA"), estimatedPnl, winRate (0-1; null = no position closed in the window, which is not measured and not 0%), tradesInWindow, unrealizedMeasured, and portraitUrl (always null for executive officials). benchmark.available false means SPY was not measured (benchmark.reason); it is not a 0% return. available false with reason "pending" means the window has not been computed yet, not that nobody traded.

window.description: Trailing window in days. Only 90 is supported (default 90).

tools.name: get_politician_roles
tools.description: Get committee leadership roles (Chair, Ranking Member, etc.) for a politician, identified by URL slug (e.g. "sen-nancy-pelosi").

tools.name: get_recent_congressional_votes
tools.description: Get recent congressional roll-call votes across all members, sourced from GovTrack (both chambers as available; currently Senate-heavy). Each vote includes member, bill info, position, and result.

tools.name: get_recently_sponsored_bills
tools.description: Get the most recently introduced bills across all congressional sponsors. Each bill includes the sponsor block (bioguideId, fullName, party, state, politicianSlug) so persona agents can link directly to the sponsor detail page. politicianSlug is null when the sponsor is no longer in the active roster (typically ex-members). Requires CONGRESS_API_KEY on the backend.

congress.description: Congress number to filter (default: 119 for current session)

tools.name: get_political_sector_rotation
tools.description: Which market sectors politicians have been trading in over a trailing window. Aggregates congressional + executive trades by sector and returns, per sector: trade count, total dollar volume, number of distinct politicians, and the top tickers, showing where political trading activity is concentrating (e.g. "politicians piled into Energy this month"). Sortable by count or dollar volume.

sortBy.description: Rank sectors by trade count or summed dollar volume (default: count)

chamber.description: Optional chamber filter (default: all chambers merged)

tools.name: get_senate_trades_by_ticker
tools.description: Reverse lookup: which politicians recently traded a given ticker. Returns recent STOCK Act disclosures for that symbol with politician info, transaction type, and amount.

tools.name: get_cash_position
tools.description: Signal8 cash position model for a company, derived from the dilution snapshot pipeline: anchor cash and anchor date, monthly burn, post-anchor capital raises (with SEC filing citations), known outflows, estimated current cash and runway months. Returns HTTP 200 for unavailable data; the `available` and `reason` fields say why. Coverage is partial: `available: false` with reason `snapshot_not_generated` means this company has not been analysed yet, which is different from it having no cash data and different from an outage (an outage is a 5xx). An unavailable response says nothing about whether the company has cash or runway. The `scenarios` envelope is kept for compatibility but only `scenarios.closed` is populated: `pending` and `announced` are null with reason `scenario_not_modelled`, because the extraction records only realized cash-raising events and does not model speculative raises; shelf or ATM capacity is not a modelled raise. Currency: amounts are in the filer's reporting currency, which is not always USD (Canadian, European, Japanese and Chinese filers report in their own currency). Top-level `currency` is ISO 4217 (null = not determined), and `currencySource: "presumed_usd"` means no foreign-currency marker was found, not a measurement. Every money object is {usd, native: {amount, currency}}: `usd` (and scenarios.closed.estimatedCashUsd / adjustedEstimatedCashUsd / netCapitalRaisesUsd) is null when the block is not in USD, and nothing is converted, so `native.amount` is in `native.currency`, not dollars. monthsOfCashLeft is currency-neutral and stays populated. Included in Signal8 Pro: without it the call returns 403 FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE with `requiredTier: "pro"` (a tier upgrade; there is no add-on to buy).

tools.name: get_cash_history
tools.description: Up to 10 years of quarterly cash and cash equivalents for a company, as reported in its SEC XBRL financial statements (data.sec.gov). Returns `history`: one point per period end {periodEnd, usd, formType, isAnnual}, oldest first. When a 10-K and a 10-Q cover the same date, the annual figure is kept. Works for any company that files XBRL financials with the SEC. Only figures reported in US dollars are included, so a filer that reports in another currency returns an empty history: an empty history means not measured, never zero cash.

tools.name: screen_must_raise
tools.description: Companies with imminent capital raise needs based on estimated cash runway. Defaults to companies with less than 6 months of cash remaining, sorted by urgency (lowest runway first): distressed companies, imminent dilution situations and potential financing catalysts. Runway is estimated from the current burn rate. Companies whose estimated cash is already exhausted are included by default and listed first: they carry cash_runway_months null with cashRunwayReason "estimate_would_be_negative" (the last cash figure, dated cashRunwayAsOf, rolled forward by the burn rate is below zero today). That is an estimate from a dated balance (estimated exhausted as of today, from the last cash figure as of cashRunwayAsOf), not a reported zero balance and not a statement that the company has no cash. Rows also carry estimatedCurrentCash / estimatedCashAsOf (dilution-snapshot cash projection; null = not measured) and listingMarket.

maxMonths.description: Maximum months of cash runway to filter by (default: 6)

includeExhausted.description: Include companies whose estimated cash is already exhausted (default: true)

market.description: Listing market: "otc" (OTC Markets) or "exchange" (NASDAQ / NYSE / NYSE American / Arca / Cboe)

industry.description: Filter by company industry (exact match, e.g. "Biotechnology", "Software")

tools.name: get_cash_runway_calendar
tools.description: Companies projected to run out of cash within a date window, a cash-depletion counterpart to a lockup expiration calendar. Returns companies sorted by urgency (lowest runway first). Runway is an estimate based on the current burn rate; actual depletion depends on future capital raises and operational changes. The default window is today to 90 days out. When the window starts today or earlier it also lists, first, companies whose estimated cash is already exhausted (cash_runway_months null, cashRunwayReason "estimate_would_be_negative", cashRunwayAsOf = the date of the cash figure that was rolled forward): an estimate, not a reported zero balance.

industry.description: Filter by company industry (exact match, e.g. "Biotechnology")

market.description: Listing market: "otc" (OTC Markets) or "exchange" (NASDAQ / NYSE / NYSE American / Arca / Cboe)

tools.name: get_dilution_coverage
tools.description: Coverage pre-check for whether Signal8 holds a dilution analysis for a company (a lighter read than the full dilution payloads): coverage status (verified / stale / not_covered), extraction state (never_extracted / running / failed / timeout / complete), last attempt and last success timestamps, the coverage tier, and whether the ticker is out of scope. `outOfScope` is a statement about the product (dilution analysis covers small-cap issuers only) and says nothing about that company's dilution. `stale` means the analysis is real but predates recent filings; `statusDetail` refines it: `newer_filing_unread` (`unreadFilings` names the material filings since: new or amended instrument, 424B5 pricing, split, 10-K) or `delisting_filed` (`delistingFiled` names the Form 25/25-NSE/15). A stale analysis describes the company as it stood before that filing, not as of today. A null `unreadFilings` means not measured, not "nothing filed since". Returns HTTP 200 for unavailable data; the `available` and `reason` fields say why. `not_covered` means this company has not been analysed yet, not that it has no dilution; an outage is a 5xx. A null, absent or withheld value means the figure was not measured; it does not mean "no dilution", "no warrants", "no shelf" or zero. A numeric 0 is a measured zero, so availability is carried by the availability, withheld and reason fields, not by the value. Included in Signal8 Pro: without it the call returns 403 FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE with `requiredTier: "pro"` (a tier upgrade; there is no add-on to buy).

tools.name: get_dilution_risk
tools.description: Dilution pressure score: 0-100 with a seven-component breakdown (shelf capacity, ATM/equity-line capacity, warrants in the money, convertible proximity, cash burn urgency, historical dilution, toxic financing), plus four risk levels: overall, offering ability, overhead supply, cash need. Score: components whose inputs could not be measured are dropped from the denominator, so `score` is out of `scoreMaxMeasured`, not out of 100 (58 may be 58 out of 85), and `scoreUnmeasuredComponents` names the excluded components. A low numerator over a reduced denominator is not a low-risk reading. `scoreDenominatorThin: true` (under 70 measured points) marks a partial reading (N of M measured). A non-null `scoreWithheldReason` (e.g. `no_dilution_snapshot`) means there is no score, not a score of zero. With no filed share count, the share-count and market-cap components rest on `details.sharesOutstandingEstimate` {shares, kind, asOf, source}, and `details.marketCapSource` is `"derived_price_x_estimated_os"`: those components rest on an estimate. Levels: when `levelsAreLowerBound` (always present) is true, the levels named in `levelsLowerBoundScope` are a lower bound (floors), not measurements: "medium" means at least medium. Levels outside that scope are measured. `levelsLowerBoundReason` determines which levels are floored: `unquantified_live_instruments` floors overall and overheadSupply; `offering_capacity_unknown` and `market_cap_unmeasured` floor overall and offeringAbility, not `overheadSupply`; `os_growth_span_short`, `os_growth_issuance_floor` and `os_growth_rebased_partial` floor historical and overall; `overhead_capacity_unquantified` floors overheadSupply and overall. `details.levelBounds` per level: `floor` (unsized instruments at zero), `ceiling` (at filed maximum; null when some instrument has none), `exact`, `bestEstimate`, `estimated`, `estimateBasis`. An estimated level is a best estimate between its floor and ceiling, not a measurement. A null `overall` with a non-null `levelsWithheldReason` is withheld, not low. `offeringAbility` is a capability profile, not pressure today: a live ATM or equity line with a measured $0 drawable (e.g. clamped by the I.B.6 cap) reads medium while the score prices the $0, and it does not mean the company cannot raise. `atmRemainingBasis` / `elocRemainingBasis` values `total_minus_reported_sales` and `total_no_sales_reported` mark "up to" figures. `overheadSupply` is potential dilution excluding shelf as a % of shares outstanding: warrants, convertibles and preferred at gross counts, plus live ATM remaining (baby-shelf clamped) and equity-line remaining at the current price, plus live S-1 shares, plus `details.registeredResaleOverhangShares`. Low up to 20%, Medium 20-50%, High over 50%. `details.overheadSupplyBasis` itemises the components (null = not measured) and `unquantified`; it is not the treasury-netted `inTheMoneySupplyPct` / `totalDilutiveShares`. When `details.osGrowthRate` is null, `details.osGrowthFacts` {fromShares, fromDate, toShares, toDate, splitsInWindow, basis} is a fact, not a rating; with `basis: "as_filed"` the two counts are on different split bases and are not a growth comparison. Returns HTTP 200 for unavailable data; the `available` and `reason` fields say why. `not_covered` means this company has not been analysed yet, not that it has no dilution; an outage is a 5xx. A null, absent or withheld value means the figure was not measured; it does not mean "no dilution", "no warrants", "no shelf" or zero. A numeric 0 is a measured zero, so availability is carried by the availability, withheld and reason fields, not by the value. Figures are as of `meta.asOfDate`, from filings read through `meta.filingsThrough` (a stale date predates anything filed since). Share counts are on one split basis; a row that cannot be rebased is omitted and counted rather than published on a mixed basis. Included in Signal8 Pro: without it the call returns 403 FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE with `requiredTier: "pro"` (a tier upgrade; there is no add-on to buy).

annotations.title: Get Dilution Pressure Score and Risk Levels

tools.name: get_dilution_snapshot
tools.description: Dilution snapshot header (the largest dilution payload): summary totals (potential new shares, their % of shares outstanding, per-family totals), the cash position (anchor cash, monthly burn, estimated current cash, runway months), the float block, and `meta` provenance. Instrument rows are not included. Cash is in the filer's reporting currency: `cashPosition.currency` is ISO 4217 (null = not determined), and `cashPosition.currencySource: "presumed_usd"` is a presumption, not a measurement. Runway months are currency-neutral. Float: a non-null `floatWithheldReason` means the tradeable float was not measured, and no float figure is stated. A declined float block (`available: false`) may carry `refusal.withheldReason`, the same value the standalone float data serves. `tradeableFloatCeiling` is an upper bound, not a float: the float is at most that figure, and the ceiling is not an input to a market capitalisation, percent-of-float, short-interest ratio or comparison. Bounded totals: a null total (`potentialNewShares`, `totalWarrantShares`, `totalConvertibleShares`, `totalEquityPlanShares`, `totalExchangeableShares`, `totalRightsShares`, `potentialDilutionPercent`) may sit beside `<key>Bound: "ceiling"`, `<key>Ceiling` and `<key>Floor`: the total is at most the ceiling, the floor is the measured part, and the ceiling is not the total. With `potentialDilutionPercentBoundReason: "stated_count_denominator"` there is no floor: the ceiling divides by the last stated share count (as of `potentialDilutionPercentCeilingShareCountAsOf`), so the figure is at most that percentage against the count stated as of that date. Approximate totals: `<total>Approximate: true` (e.g. `potentialNewSharesApproximate`, `potentialDilutionPercentApproximate`, `totalWarrantSharesApproximate`) means that total includes an issuer-stated approximate count ("approximately 16.1 million shares"): state it as approximately / ≈ that figure, never as exact. `statedCountSizedRows[]` lists every row sized from its own cited filing text (rule, shares, approximate, quote, accession). `notMeasuredReasons[]` ({field, code, text, detail, expected {form, dueDate, status}}) gives the reason a figure is null; it is an explanation, not a value. `expectedFilings[]` lists the next periodic report(s): `status: "late"` means due by `dueDate` with none on file as of `checkedOn` and carries no information about why; `dueDate: null` means not computed. A `kind: "annual_meeting"` row (Nasdaq 5620(a) / NYSE 302.00) with status "late" means no 8-K Item 5.07 vote results are on file, not that a meeting was missed. SPAC rights: `totalRightsShares` (present only when the snapshot examined rights) is the shares delivered to holders of SPAC unit rights on the initial business combination; it is included in `potentialNewShares`, and the rights lapse if no combination closes. `rightsOverlapWarrantRows` > 0 means a warrant row also names rights, so the rights total and the headline are withheld (null) rather than counted twice. A runway figure beside `goingConcern: true` is a contradiction the auditors flagged: the going-concern doubt qualifies the runway. tools.name: get_rvol_history
tools.description: Get the per-day relative-volume (RVOL) time series for a ticker, bucketed by trading session (premarket 04:00-09:30 ET, regular 09:30-16:00, afterhours 16:00-20:00, or all four). Each day's RVOL compares that session's volume to a trailing same-session baseline (30 trading days by default, configurable via "baselineDays"), so premarket volume is judged against premarket history (not a stale full-day figure); the series shows unusual premarket / session volume surges over the last N days. Each point also carries "baselineState": "ready" (rvol is populated), "warming" (baseline not yet warm), "no-cutoff-history" (established ticker that never traded at this session/cutoff before) or "no-history" (new listing, no prior trading history at all), so a null rvol is explained rather than silent. Points additionally carry "advRatio" (that day's volume / the trailing 30-session average full-day volume, null when no full-day denominator exists) and "advDays" (its sample size), which give a magnitude to points RVOL cannot rate. advRatio is not an RVOL: it compares a partial session to a whole day, so it is typically well under 1 and is not comparable to rvol.

session.description: One session bucket; unset returns all four sessions.

days.description: Number of trailing calendar days of history (1–90, default 30).

asOfTime.description: Optional true time-of-day premarket basis. Any HH:MM ET premarket time; snapped to the nearest 15-minute grid cutoff (04:00–09:15, ties resolve to the earlier cutoff). When set, the series is the premarket as-of RVOL: cumulative volume known by that cutoff / the trailing baselineDays (default 30) average of the same cutoff (not the full 04:00-09:30 session). Forces the premarket session; any "session" argument is ignored. Each point carries a "basis" field: the snapped cutoff actually used ("asof-0700"), or "full-session" for dates with no precomputed as-of row. Unset means the standard full-session series.

baselineDays.description: Rolling RVOL baseline window, in trading rows (same-session days). Default 30; values outside 20-250 are clamped. This is the DENOMINATOR window: every RVOL in the response is that period's volume divided by the average of the trailing N same-session (or same-cutoff) days, excluding the day itself. A SHORTER window tracks recent regime changes faster and is noisier; a LONGER one is smoother and slower to react. The warm-up lookback scales with it automatically, so a wide window is never under-filled into an inflated ratio; the minimum-warm-days gate (20 prior sessions) does NOT scale down, so at the 30-row default a ticker needs 20 of its last 30 sessions populated before rvol is non-null. Unset means the standard 30-day baseline; 90 reproduces the pre-2026-09 window.

tools.name: get_premarket_scanner
tools.description: Get the live premarket scanner board (premarket small-cap runners): top premarket gainers and losers by absolute gap %, each row enriched with rvol, marketCap, floatShares, short interest, dilution and news/catalyst flags. Off-hours it falls back to the last session. includePennyStocks=true includes sub-$1 names. Float: floatShares is the measured point float (null on a withheld dilution-snapshot row, which then carries "floatEstimate" {shares, bound: "point" | "ceiling" | "floor", basis}). A point estimate is a number with its as-of and caveat; a ceiling or floor is a bound, not a figure: the float is not stated and is at most (ceiling) or at least (floor) that number, and is not a basis for arithmetic; neither present = not measured, not 0. The low-float board admits on that figure's value (an 8M ceiling is in, a 26M floor is out). Compliance: row "compliance", the compliance/split badges, "reverseSplitSignal" and "deficiencySignal" are Signal8 Pro; for other callers "compliance" is null with "complianceWithheld": "pro_required", meaning withheld, which is not "not measured" and not "no deficiency". Live volume (04:00-09:30 ET only; null outside the window or until the baseline is warm, never fabricated) has two different metrics, neither interchangeable with the other or with "rvol". "liveRvol" = live cumulative premarket volume / the trailing 30-session average cumulative volume at the same time of morning, with "liveRvolAsOf" the 15-minute grid cutoff (meta.asOf shows any time skew); "premarketPaceRatio" = the same volume / the trailing 30-session average full premarket session (>1.0 = already beat a normal premarket). universe="lowfloat" returns the separate low-float board (float under 10M, no top-100 slice) from the aggregator snapshot; an empty rows array with meta.reason when none is published is a normal off-hours state.

includePennyStocks.description: Include sub-$1 (penny) stocks in the results. Default false.

universe.description: Which board to return. "default" (the default) is the movers-derived top-100 board. "lowfloat" is the low-float board (float < 10M shares, no top-100 slice).

tools.name: get_upcoming_reverse_splits
tools.description: Reverse stock splits scheduled to take effect within a day-offset window of the current US market day, for companies under a market-cap ceiling. Offsets are days from today on the US market calendar: fromOffset=1, toOffset=1 is tomorrow; fromOffset=1, toOffset=7 is the week ahead. Each row carries the ticker, company name, the exact vendor integers (splitFrom/splitTo), a pre-rendered ratio ("1-for-20"), the effective date, market cap, float in shares, and price. floatShares is on the same split basis as the market cap. floatBasis says what it is: "measured", or "estimate" / "estimate_rebased" (the float ladder's point estimate, moved across this split when it predates it), i.e. an estimate rather than a measurement. floatShares: null means not measured or withheld, not zero and not "no float"; such rows are included (they have a valid market cap) and floatWithheldReason gives the reason. floatUnknownCount counts those null-float rows in the list; it is not a withholding count (withheldCount is). price is on the same split basis as the market cap (null when it cannot be stated on one basis), so it is not comparable with a pre-split price from elsewhere. Rows are splits scheduled as of now, not a guarantee that every split effective in the window is already known: the underlying stock_splits table has no created_at column, so when a row first appeared is unmeasurable, and a split announced later is simply missing. The result is "scheduled as of now", not "all" reverse splits. A scheduled split can also be postponed or cancelled after it is announced. capUnknownCount is a withholding count, not a zero: it counts rows that passed every other filter and were deliberately excluded because Signal8 has no measured market cap for them (typically real OTC microcaps). It does not mean those companies have no dilution, no split or no cap; the cap was not measured, so they cannot be asserted to sit under the stated ceiling, and with capUnknownCount above zero the list is not complete for an "under $Xm" framing. Funds, ETFs and sub-1.5x fractional ratio adjustments are already removed server-side, and the ratio is the vendor's. An empty splits array is a normal, common result: most single weekdays have no sub-cap reverse split scheduled at all. It is not an error, not a failure and not evidence that reverse-split activity has stopped. includeLifecycle=true adds Signal8's SEC-filing lifecycle tracker: top-level lifecycleAvailable, and per row `lifecycle` = the tracked episode (state, ratio, ratioRange, meetingDate, the issuer-stated effectiveDate, effectiveCondition, verification, asOf, sourceUrl). lifecycle: null means no episode tracked, not "no split" and not a contradiction of the calendar row; a row with no lifecycle key could not be matched to an SEC registrant (not measured). lifecycleAvailable: false means the tracker is switched off or unreadable, so the response carries no lifecycle information. verification "provisional" = one source, not cross-checked. Scope: this is the vendor market calendar only. The merged list the Signal8 Reverse Splits page shows (the calendar union the SEC-filing tracker, one row per security, with the stage, approval route, authority terms, source filings and the Approved-no-date / Vote-pending tabs) is a separate cross-company list.

fromOffset.description: Window start as a day offset from the US market day (default 1 = tomorrow). Must be <= toOffset; an inverted window is rejected rather than silently returning an empty list.

toOffset.description: Window end, inclusive, as a day offset from the US market day (default 1). Use 7 with fromOffset 1 for the week ahead.

includeLifecycle.description: Attach the tracked SEC-filing lifecycle episode to each row (default false). null = no episode tracked, never "no split"; a missing key = not matched to a registrant (not measured).

maxMarketCap.description: Exclusive market-cap ceiling in USD (default 300000000). Rows with NO measured market cap are excluded and counted in capUnknownCount, never assumed to be under the ceiling.

tools.name: get_recent_uplistings
tools.description: OTC-to-exchange uplistings that FINRA recorded on a given US market day, for companies under a market-cap ceiling. Each row carries the old OTC symbol, the resolved new exchange symbol (or null), a confirmed flag, the destination venue (NASDAQ / NYSE / NYSE American / ARCA), company name, effective date, market cap and float in shares. This is a same-day read and there is no forward-looking version: FINRA records an uplisting at roughly 01:45 ET on the day it becomes effective, and the source table has no scheduled or announced column. dayOffset exists for catch-up reads of past days, not for forecasting, and a positive offset returns nothing. Every row has already happened; none is upcoming or expected. newSymbol: null is a published state, not a missing field: FINRA's row names only the old OTC symbol, and the new ticker is resolved by company-name match against Nasdaq SymDir and sometimes cannot be resolved. A guessed ticker could name a company that did not uplist, so an unresolved row names the old symbol and states that the new one was not resolved; the null is not a gap to fill and the row is still a real uplisting. confirmed: false means the symbol resolution is provisional and the new ticker is not asserted as fact; only confirmed: true is a confirmed resolution. capUnknownCount is a withholding count, not a zero: rows that cleared every other filter but have no measured market cap, so they cannot be asserted to sit under the stated ceiling. It does not mean those companies have no cap, and a cap-bracketed list with capUnknownCount above zero is not complete. An empty uplistings array is the normal, expected result on most days: uplistings run roughly 6.6 per month across all market caps, so the large majority of days genuinely have none. It is not an error, not an outage and not evidence that uplisting activity has stopped.

dayOffset.description: Day offset from the US market day (default 0 = today). Negative values read past days. A positive value returns nothing: there is no forward-looking uplisting data.

maxMarketCap.description: Exclusive market-cap ceiling in USD (default 300000000). Rows with NO measured market cap are excluded and counted in capUnknownCount, never assumed to be under the ceiling.

tools.name: get_reverse_split_lifecycle
tools.description: The reverse-split lifecycle Signal8 has tracked from a company's own SEC filings (proxies, 8-K Items 3.03/5.03/5.07, 6-Ks): one episode per split authority, newest first, each with its state (proposed, vote scheduled, approved, ratio set, effective date announced, charter filed, ... or closed), the ratio or authorised range, meeting / vote / effective dates, the state history, and the events behind it oldest first. Every event carries its source (accession and an EDGAR sourceUrl) and its facts; every stated fact carries the verbatim quote it was read from. Not stated means not measured, not "no": a fact with notStated:true (or a null field) means the documents read did not say it, not that it is false, zero or absent. coverage "unresolved" means the ticker could not be matched to an SEC registrant (not measured). coverage "tracked" with an empty episodes list means no episode has been tracked from the filings read since the tracker started; it is not evidence that no reverse split is planned. effectiveDate is the date the issuer stated, strictly parsed: a scheduled date, not a confirmation that the split happened (it can be postponed or abandoned). A conditional date ("the 25th trading day after the Trigger Event") is returned verbatim in effectiveCondition and is not a date; no date is computed from it. verification is copied from the tracker: "provisional" = one source, not cross-checked (the default, not "doubtful"); "verified" = cross-checked. Approval (present only when approvalAvailable is true): each episode carries approvalPath {path, label, quote, sourceUrl}: shareholder_vote, written_consent, fpi_written_resolution, pre_approved_range (the board set the ratio inside a range shareholders approved earlier), board_only (the company's own filing states no shareholder approval was required, quoted), depositary_ratio_change (an ADS ratio change by the depositary, no shareholder vote, the ordinary shares not consolidated) or unknown. The response also carries domicile {code, label, group, source} (EDGAR, else the latest 10-K / 20-F cover; null = not measured, not "Delaware") and splitAuthority {authority, basis, label, boardMayActWithoutVote, conditions, statute, quote, sourceUrl}. Only basis own_prior_board_only_announcement or charter_clause is board split authority on file: a charter clause is a standing power; own prior evidence is a PAST board-only split (dated in the label, conditional on its statute, e.g. NRS 78.207 needs authorized shares cut by the same ratio), not a power to skip a vote now, and the current split can still go to a vote. authority "unknown" or basis "domicile_default_only" is not a finding about the company: it only states what the domicile's law allows by default (e.g. "Domicile may permit board action; charter not checked"), not that this company can split without a vote. vote_required appears only as a labelled domicile default, not as a statement that a vote is needed. path "unknown" is not "no vote"; a missing proxy does not determine a path. An HTTP 503 FEATURE_DISABLED means the lifecycle tracker is switched off and the response says nothing about the company's splits.

tools.name: get_ended_reverse_splits

Null means not measured or not stated. An empty list is what the tracker has on file for the window, not evidence that no company abandoned a split; completeness "tracked_episodes" = what the tracker has read from filings since it started, not every company. boundReached: true = the window held more episodes than one read returns (a narrower from / to window returns the rest). Locked rows are withheld, not absent. The facts are part of Signal8 Pro: a key not owned by a Pro account gets rows with locked: true and only ticker, companyName, hasPage and exchange (access "preview", lockedCount); a locked row means the facts were withheld from this caller. outcome, from and to are Pro-only filters: on a non-Pro key they apply to unlocked rows only and locked rows are left out (filtersLimitedToUnlocked: true). exchange applies to every row. Paging uses limit and the nextCursor of the previous response (null = last page). available: false (reason "tracker_not_enabled") = the tracker is switched off; an HTTP 503 FEATURE_DISABLED = the Reverse Splits page is switched off. tools.name: get_reverse_split_authority
tools.description: Companies whose board still holds reverse-split authority it may use without another shareholder vote: an approval on file (shareholder vote or written consent; tracker states consent_pending, voted_approved, ratio_fixed) not past a stated expiry, one row per company (its newest approval; other live ones in otherLiveAuthorityEpisodeIds). Soonest stated expiry first. Each row is the Reverse Splits page row (ticker, companyName, ratio, exchange, approvalPath, domicile, splitAuthority, authorityTerms, sourceUrl / sourceAccession, sourceDocuments: every document behind the approval with accession or URL) plus an "authority" block: episodeId, state, approvedDate, approvedRatio {fixed, min, max} (the per-split ratio or range approved), cumulativeCap (cap on the product of every split drawn on it), multiStep, expiresOn, expiryTerm, daysUntilExpiry, and room: capRatio + capBasis ("cumulative_cap", or "single_split_maximum" = no cumulative cap stated and nothing drawn, so one split up to the approved maximum), perSplitMax, usedSplits + usedRatio (product of the splits already executed on it; 1 = none drawn), remainingRatio (capRatio / usedRatio), exhausted, nextSplitMax, pendingRatio (a ratio the board set that has not taken effect) and a one-line label. The approval route is approvalPath.path (shareholder_vote, written_consent, fpi_written_resolution, pre_approved_range, board_only, depositary_ratio_change or unknown = "Not determined", not "no vote"). Ratios are 1-for-N factors and combine by product. Not measured is not "none remaining": room.remainingRatio null comes with room.notMeasuredReason ("cumulative_cap_not_stated", "ratio_not_stated" or "drawn_split_ratio_not_stated"), meaning the remaining room is not measured for that reason. Such rows are listed, never dropped, and are not full. expiresOn null = the documents read state no expiry, not "never expires". An empty list is what the tracker has on file, not evidence that no board holds authority. This screen covers approvals on file; a board that may split under its statute or charter with no approval at all shows as splitAuthority.boardMayActWithoutVote on a row and in the per-company lifecycle, and is not listed here on that basis alone. Locked rows are withheld, not absent. A row whose remaining room or expiry is not measured never matches those filters; excludedNotMeasured counts how many were left out for that reason. Paging uses limit and nextCursor. available: false or an HTTP 503 FEATURE_DISABLED = unavailable, and the response says nothing about any company. The data describes what is on file and carries no view on whether a split will happen, what it means for the price, or what anyone should do.

tools.name: get_reverse_splits_list
tools.description: The cross-company reverse-split lists the Signal8 Reverse Splits page serves, one view per call. view "upcoming" = splits with an effective date from tomorrow through 30 US market days ahead, the vendor market calendar union Signal8's SEC-filing tracker (filings, exchange and depositary notices); "recent" = the same union for effective dates in the past 30 days; "approved_no_date" = tracked episodes where shareholders (or the board, where no vote is required) have approved a reverse split but no effective date is stated yet; "vote_pending" = tracked episodes where a reverse split is proposed and the shareholder vote has not happened yet; "cancelled" = tracked episodes that ended without the split taking effect in the past 90 days (withdrawn by the company, a vote that did not approve it, an approved authority that expired unused, a meeting postponed indefinitely), with a cancelled object (outcome, outcomeLabel, endedOn, endedOnBasis, laterEpisode when the company has a newer open proposal) and the closing document as the source; older ended episodes are on the separate ended-reverse-splits tool. A security sits on exactly one of the first four views (upcoming, then recent, then approved_no_date, then vote_pending), with one exception: a split the company's own filing dates is on upcoming even when the same company also has a different, later split proposal awaiting a vote, which is then on vote_pending too; "cancelled" may repeat a company another view lists. Each row carries ticker, companyName, hasPage, source ("market_calendar" or "tracker"), stage + stageLabel, trackerState, ratio (or ratioMin / ratioMax for an authorised range), meetingDate, approvedDate, effectiveDate, effectiveDateSource, marketCalendarAgrees / marketCalendarDate / marketCalendarRatio, effectiveCondition, verification, marketConfirmation (recent only), marketCapUsd + capBucket, securityType, exchange, cik, sourceUrl / sourceAccession / sourceFormType / sourceFiledDate / sourceLabel, sourceDocuments (every document behind the episode), quote, adsRatioChange, approvalPath, domicile, splitAuthority and authorityTerms. Null means not measured or not stated: not "no split", not zero, not "no vote needed" and not "no date". A null ratio = the documents state none yet; a null marketCapUsd = cap not measured (capBucket is then null, not "nano"); a null verification = no tracked episode; a null domicile = not measured (not "Delaware"); a null marketConfirmation = the price step was not measured. An empty rows array on a view is normal and is not evidence that no company is splitting. completeness says what the view is: "scheduled_as_of_now" (upcoming) and "recorded_as_of_now" (recent) are what is known as of now, not "all reverse splits"; "tracked_episodes" is what the tracker has read from filings since it started, not every company. A scheduled split can still be postponed or cancelled: it is scheduled, not confirmed. Dates: effectiveDate is the scheduled effective date (vendor calendar, or the issuer-stated date strictly parsed from the filing); a filing or listing-rule deadline is not an effective date and does not appear in this field. A conditional date ("the 25th trading day after...") is returned verbatim in effectiveCondition and is not a date. effectiveDateSource says where effectiveDate came from: "filing" = the issuer stated it; "market_calendar" = the filing states no date and the vendor calendar supplies it. marketCalendarAgrees is a cross-check on a tracker row the calendar also lists: true = same date and ratio; false = at least one differs and marketCalendarDate / marketCalendarRatio hold the calendar's value (the filing's value is the row's value, and the two sources disagree); null or absent = not compared (no calendar row). meetingDate is the shareholder meeting date, not the split date. Approval and authority: approvalPath.path is shareholder_vote, written_consent, fpi_written_resolution, pre_approved_range (the board sets the ratio inside a range shareholders approved earlier), board_only (the issuer's own filing says no shareholder approval is required, quoted), depositary_ratio_change (an ADS ratio change by the depositary, no vote) or unknown ("Not determined", not "no vote"). splitAuthority.boardMayActWithoutVote is true only from the issuer's own filing or charter; a domicile default alone is not a finding. authorityTerms is the authority behind the episode: a cumulativeCap (the board may split in steps, each within the cap, without a new vote until the authority expires), multiStep, the expiry, and what executed splits already used; null = the documents state nothing beyond the ratio. Locked rows are withheld, not absent. The split facts on every view are part of Signal8 Pro. A caller whose API key is not owned by a Pro account gets every row with locked: true and only ticker, companyName, hasPage and exchange on it; the response then carries access: "preview", lockedCount (how many rows are locked) and rowLimit. A locked row means the facts exist and were not shown to this caller (they need Signal8 Pro); it does not mean "no split". access: "full" = every row carries its facts. filtersLimitedToUnlocked: true = a board / domicile filter was applied to unlocked rows only (locked rows are left out entirely, because matching them would reveal the fact through membership). Filters apply server-side: cap (scanner buckets), type (security type), exchange, board ("without_vote": board split authority on file, from the issuer's own filing or charter) and domicile. Each accepts "not_measured" to select rows where that fact was not measured; an unmeasured row never matches a measured bucket. totalCount is the filtered list (locked rows included), unfilteredCount the view before filters, capUnknownCount the rows whose cap was not measured (on the calendar views). Paging uses limit / offset; truncated: true = more rows exist. available: false with reason "tracker_not_enabled" (the three tracker views) means the tracker is switched off, not that nothing is pending. An HTTP 503 FEATURE_DISABLED means the page is switched off, and the response then says nothing about any company's split. The data describes what is on file and carries no view on whether a split will happen, what it means for the price, or what anyone should do.

view.description: Which list: "upcoming" (effective tomorrow through 30 market days ahead; the calendar UNION the tracker), "recent" (effective in the past 30 days), "approved_no_date" (approved, no effective date stated yet), "vote_pending" (proposed; the shareholder vote has not happened), "cancelled" (ended without taking effect in the past 90 days). Default "upcoming".

cap.description: Market-cap buckets to keep (the premarket scanner's): nano, micro, small, mid, large, or not_measured for rows whose cap was not measured. Empty = every row.

type.description: Security types to keep: common, adr (ADR / ADS), ordinary (foreign ordinary shares), other, or not_measured. Empty = every row.

exchange.description: Listing venues to keep: NASDAQ, NYSE, AMEX (NYSE American), OTC, or not_measured. Empty = every row.

instructions:
Signal8 provides read-only SEC-filing intelligence and market data for US-listed companies, plus US congressional and executive-branch (STOCK Act) trading and FEC campaign-finance data.

Typical workflow:
- Resolve a company with `search_companies` (name or ticker), then use the company tools: `get_company_profile`, `get_quote`, `get_financials`, `get_short_interest`, `get_float` (latest) and `get_float_history` (past dates), `get_earnings`, insider trades (`get_insiders`) and ownership (`get_institutions`, `get_ownership`). Most tools take a bare ticker (e.g. "AAPL"). Prefer `get_stock_price_change` before full candles from `get_historical_prices`. `get_news` is per company; `get_market_news` is market-wide. Halt rows from `get_trading_halts` carry no price (use `get_quote`).
- Lists and counts of companies by market cap, price or float: `screen_companies`. Filings by sector: `screen_sec_filings`; by form, date, item, text or company filters: `search_sec_filings` (`search_filing_text` returns matching passages). A row `id` or a `lookup_accession_number` `filingId` feeds `get_filing_document` (whole submission) and `get_filing_exhibits`; `get_filing_documents` lists every document with an `exhibitId` for `get_exhibit_content`. `get_filing_structured` parses Forms 3/4/5, 13F and 13D/G. A search starting before `archiveFrom` is outside the archive, not evidence that no filing exists.
- Small-cap dilution: call `get_dilution_coverage` first (`not_covered` means not analysed yet, not "no dilution"), then `get_dilution_risk`, `get_dilution_snapshot` (totals, cash, float; no rows) and `get_dilution_instruments` with one family per call. `get_baby_shelf_capacity` is the live raisable-now figure (the stored shelf capacity on instrument rows is dated). `get_dilution_performance`, `get_dilution_history`, `get_cash_position`, `get_cash_history`, `get_cash_runway_calendar` and `screen_must_raise` cover the rest. The `explain_dilution` prompt runs the whole workflow.
- Reverse splits: `get_reverse_splits_list` (merged calendar + SEC tracker, one view per call), `get_upcoming_reverse_splits` (vendor calendar only), `get_reverse_split_lifecycle` (one company, with quotes and source links to cite), `get_ended_reverse_splits`, `get_reverse_split_authority`, `get_split_history` and `get_split_performance` (past splits only).
- Institutions take a CIK from `get_institutions` or `search_institutions`; `get_institution_position_changes` is the server-side quarter diff, and `get_institution_top_aum` the full AUM list. `get_insider_cross_company` is the market-wide counterpart of `get_insiders`. `get_premarket_scan_history` uses the same RVOL math as `get_rvol_history`; with `asOfTime`, check `meta.asOfApplied` on every response.
- Politicians: resolve the slug (e.g. `sen-nancy-pelosi`) with `get_politicians`, then `get_politician_transactions`, `get_senate_trades_by_ticker` and the other politician tools. P&L figures are estimates; use full titles and party/state words. Late filings are late, not "illegal". For `get_politician_disclosures` polling, send `nextCursor` back as `since` and keep calling while `hasMore`. Donors: `get_politician_donor_summary` (top 10, cycle totals), `get_politician_donors` (full list), `get_donor_aggregates` (market-wide). Trade-event overlap tools give transaction and disclosure dates together.
- To explain a concept or term, use the free Signal8 Academy tools (`search_learn_guides`, then `get_learn_guide`; `define_term` for jargon, falling back to `search_learn_guides` on TERM_NOT_FOUND) and cite the guide url. They need no Signal8 API key or Pro plan (on the hosted server, any signed-in account).

Calls are metered by the caller's API-key tier, so batch intent into the most specific tool rather than many broad calls.

Reporting rules:
- A null, withheld, locked or unavailable figure means not measured (or not shown to this caller), never "no dilution", "none" or zero. Quote `notMeasuredReasons` / `withheldReason` text rather than turning it into a value. A locked row means the facts need Signal8 Pro.
- Bounded figures stay bounded: a ceiling is "at most X", a floor or lower-bound level is "at least X", in words with no ~ / <= / >= glyph. Report a dilution score as `score` out of `scoreMaxMeasured`, naming the unmeasured components; never rescale it to 100.
- State the as-of date with every figure (share counts, float, cash, quotes). A stale analysis "predates" the newer filing it names.
- Lists are what is on file as of now ("scheduled as of now"), not "all"; an empty list is a normal result, and `capUnknownCount` / `excludedNotMeasured` rows were left out for unmeasured data, so disclose the count with any cap-bracketed framing.
- An unresolved `newSymbol` or an unconfirmed resolution stays unresolved / provisional; do not fill it in. Do not substitute a vendor float for a withheld one, or compute percent-of-float from a bound or estimate.
- When a 403 FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE or HTTP 503 FEATURE_DISABLED comes back, say the data is unavailable to this account or switched off, and say nothing about the company.
- Describe history as history. Give no price predictions and no buy or sell advice; a match between trades and events is not evidence of wrongdoing.
